knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the positive-semidefinite completion form of chordal decomposition for sparse lifted matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal, with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), and let \(X\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose specified positions are the diagonal and the edges of \(G\). There exists a completed matrix \(\widehat X\in\mathbb S^{|V|}_+\) satisfying \(\widehat X_{ij}=X_{ij}\) at every specified position if and only if
\[
X[C_k,C_k]\succeq0\qquad(k=1,\ldots,m).
\]
Thus a sparse Shor constraint may be represented by positive-semidefinite constraints on maximal-clique submatrices, provided shared entries represent one common partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, a partial matrix has a positive-semidefinite completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal submatrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Chordal PSD Decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-semidefinite completion theorem is mathematically standard, stated with the necessary chordality and specified-entry hypotheses, and fits the Chordal PSD Decomposition leaf. However, the record has no citation or inspectable locator, so its theorem statement cannot pass source review.

assumptions_latex: The maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\) are those of a chordal graph.
Each local matrix \(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}\) is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise agreement on clique overlaps defines a common partial matrix having a positive-semidefinite completion.

notation.meaning: Local matrix for maximal clique k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: overlap equality is the consistency condition in chordal sparse SDP formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the overlap constraints coupling local clique matrices in a sparse Shor relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), local matrices \(X^{(k)}\in\mathbb S^{|C_k|}_+\) are clique-consistent when, for every pair with \(S_{k\ell}=C_k\cap C_\ell\neq\varnothing\),
\[
X^{(k)}[S_{k\ell},S_{k\ell}]=X^{(\ell)}[S_{k\ell},S_{k\ell}].
\]
These equalities make all copies of each specified entry identical and therefore define one partial symmetric matrix \(X\). If the clique family comes from a chordal graph, clique positivity together with these consistency equalities implies that \(X\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion. Omitting an overlap equality generally enlarges the sparse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clique matrices must assign identical values to every shared entry. With chordal cliques and local positive semidefiniteness, this consistency yields a globally completable partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Consistency Relaxations

assumptions_latex: The lifted Shor matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\) would ordinarily satisfy \(Y\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Imposing positive semidefiniteness only on all \(2\times2\) principal submatrices gives an SOCP-representable outer approximation of \(\mathbb S^n_+\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: two-by-two principal PSD constraints have a rotated-SOC representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers the pairwise second-order-cone surrogate for a Shor positive-semidefinite constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Replace \(Y\succeq0\) by
\[
Y_{ii}\ge0,\qquad Y_{jj}\ge0,\qquad Y_{ij}^{2}\le Y_{ii}Y_{jj}
\quad(1\le i<j\le n).
\]
Each inequality is equivalently the second-order-cone constraint
\[
\left\|(2Y_{ij},Y_{ii}-Y_{jj})\right\|_2\le Y_{ii}+Y_{jj}.
\]
Every positive-semidefinite \(Y\) satisfies these constraints because its \(2\times2\) principal submatrices are positive semidefinite. Consequently, substituting them for \(Y\succeq0\) enlarges the lifted feasible region and yields an SOCP relaxation of the Shor formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring every two-by-two principal submatrix to be positive semidefinite is second-order-cone representable and gives an outer approximation of the full PSD constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: SOCP Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pairwise principal-minor constraints, their second-order-cone representation, and the outer-approximation direction are correct and fit an SOCP-relaxation representation. No source or locator is supplied.

assumptions_latex: The lifted matrix is symmetric: \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Diagonal dominance is a linear sufficient condition for \(Y\succeq0\), so replacing the PSD cone by this cone produces an LP-representable conic surrogate.

notation.meaning: Cone of symmetric diagonally dominant matrices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: symmetric diagonally dominant matrices with nonnegative diagonal are positive semidefinite
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the LP-representable diagonally dominant inner approximation of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The diagonally dominant cone is
\[
\mathrm{DD}_n=\left\{Y\in\mathbb S^n:Y_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}|Y_{ij}|\ \text{for every }i\right\}.
\]
It has the linear extended formulation
\[
t_{ij}\ge Y_{ij},\quad t_{ij}\ge-Y_{ij},\quad
Y_{ii}\ge\sum_{j\ne i}t_{ij},\quad t_{ij}=t_{ji}\ge0.
\]
Every \(Y\in\mathrm{DD}_n\) is positive semidefinite, hence \(\mathrm{DD}_n\subseteq\mathbb S^n_+\). Replacing a Shor PSD constraint by \(Y\in\mathrm{DD}_n\) is therefore a tractable LP cone substitution; whether it gives an upper or lower optimization bound depends on the primal or dual placement of the cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetric diagonal dominance is expressible by linear inequalities and implies positive semidefiniteness, providing an LP-representable inner approximation of the PSD cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonally Dominant Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The DD cone definition, linear extended formulation, and inclusion in the PSD cone are standard and internally consistent. The record appropriately avoids claiming a universal objective-bound direction, but it still lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

assumptions_latex: The lifted matrix is symmetric: \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Scaled diagonal dominance is SOCP representable and satisfies \(\mathrm{DD}_n\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}_n\subseteq\mathbb S^n_+\).

notation.meaning: Cone of scaled diagonally dominant matrices
Embedding of a two-by-two block on indices i and j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scaled diagonal dominance equals a sum of embedded two-by-two PSD blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard factor-width-two representation of scaled diagonally dominant matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A matrix \(Y\in\mathbb S^n\) is scaled diagonally dominant when there exists a positive diagonal matrix \(D\succ0\) such that \(DYD\in\mathrm{DD}_n\). Equivalently,
\[
Y=\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}E_{ij}^{\mathsf T}M^{ij}E_{ij},
\qquad M^{ij}\in\mathbb S^2_+,
\]
where \(E_{ij}\) selects coordinates \(i,j\). Since each \(2\times2\) positive-semidefinite constraint is second-order-cone representable, membership in \(\mathrm{SDD}_n\) is SOCP representable. The cone inclusions are
\[
\mathrm{DD}_n\subseteq\mathrm{SDD}_n\subseteq\mathbb S^n_+.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix is scaled diagonally dominant if a positive diagonal scaling makes it diagonally dominant; equivalently, it is a sum of embedded two-by-two PSD matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Diagonally Dominant Relaxations

assumptions_latex: The exact lifted matrix is \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\) for a vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Retaining \(x\ge0\) and replacing \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \(Y\succeq0\) and entrywise \(Y\ge0\) gives a valid convex relaxation of the exact lift.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: doubly nonnegative means PSD and entrywise nonnegative
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies when the QCQP variables are constrained to be nonnegative, so their exact lifted products are entrywise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The doubly nonnegative cone is
\[
\mathrm{DNN}_n=\left\{Y\in\mathbb S^n:Y\succeq0,\ Y_{ij}\ge0\ \text{for all }i,j\right\}.
\]
If \(x\in\mathbb R^n_+\), then the exact lift \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\) belongs to \(\mathrm{DNN}_n\). Therefore retaining \(x\ge0\) and the remaining lifted linear constraints while replacing the nonconvex equality \(Y=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \(Y\in\mathrm{DNN}_n\) gives a valid convex relaxation. Relative to the ordinary Shor relaxation with the same constraints on \(x\), entrywise nonnegativity of \(Y\) strengthens the lifted formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonnegative variables, every exact rank-one lift is PSD and entrywise nonnegative. Retaining variable nonnegativity and enforcing both matrix properties strengthens the ordinary Shor relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Doubly Nonnegative Relaxations

assumptions_latex: The bounds are finite and ordered: \(\ell_x<u_x\) and \(\ell_y<u_y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Four McCormick inequalities describe exactly the convex hull of the bilinear graph over the rectangle.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds for x
Lower and upper bounds for y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the exact convex hull for one bilinear term on a bounded rectangle.

source_refs.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in[\ell_x,u_x]\), \(y\in[\ell_y,u_y]\), and \(w=xy\), the convex hull of the graph is given by the bounds on \(x,y\) and
\[
\begin{aligned}
w&\ge \ell_x y+\ell_y x-\ell_x\ell_y,\\
w&\ge u_x y+u_y x-u_xu_y,\\
w&\le u_x y+\ell_y x-u_x\ell_y,\\
w&\le \ell_x y+u_y x-\ell_xu_y.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, replacing each bounded bilinear equality by these four inequalities gives its tightest possible convex polyhedral relaxation when that term is considered in isolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Four McCormick inequalities give the exact convex hull of one bilinear product over a bounded rectangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular Bilinear Envelopes

source_witnesses.locator: 7.2 Bilinear Programming Problems p. 69

assumptions_latex: The scalar bilinear function is \(w=x^{\mathsf T}Ay\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex hull of the graph is the projection of a simplex of vertex-pair weights \(\lambda_{ij}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bilinear graphs over products of simplices are generated by vertex pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the product-of-standard-simplices version of a simplicial bilinear envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\Delta_p\), \(y\in\Delta_q\), and \(w=x^{\mathsf T}Ay\), where \(A=(a_{ij})\). The convex hull of this graph is the projection of
\[
\lambda_{ij}\ge0,
\quad \sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_{ij}=1,
\quad x_i=\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_{ij},
\quad y_j=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_{ij},
\quad w=\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{j=1}^q a_{ij}\lambda_{ij}.
\]
Thus the envelope is polyhedral in the lifted vertex-pair weights and is exact for the convex hull over the product of the two simplices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a product of simplices, the bilinear graph's convex hull is represented by nonnegative weights on pairs of simplex vertices.
knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial Bilinear Envelopes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For the expressly stated product-of-standard-simplices variant, the vertex-pair-weight formulation is mathematically coherent and exact. The taxonomy title could cover other simplicial variants, and no source is supplied to confirm that this is the intended local version.

assumptions_latex: The base relaxation is \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\) with finite bounds.
Every quadratic monomial \(x_ix_j\) is replaced by a symmetric lifted variable \(X_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearizing products of each base inequality with each nonnegative bound factor yields a valid first-level RLT relaxation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: first-level RLT multiplies valid inequalities by nonnegative bound factors and linearizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the bounded continuous-variable first-level RLT construction for a QCQP lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(P=\{x:Ax\ge b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), introduce \(X_{ij}\) for \(x_ix_j\). For every row \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r\ge0\) and coordinate \(j\), form the valid quadratic inequalities
\[
(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r)(x_j-\ell_j)\ge0,
\qquad
(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r)(u_j-x_j)\ge0.
\]
Also form products of pairs of nonnegative bound factors. Apply the linearization map \(\mathcal L(x_ix_j)=X_{ij}\), retain the original linear constraints, and optimize over the resulting polyhedron in \((x,X)\). Any exact lift \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) is feasible, so the construction is a valid relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-level RLT multiplies each valid linear inequality by nonnegative variable-bound factors and replaces every resulting quadratic monomial with a lifted variable.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Level RLT Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is a valid bounded continuous-variable RLT procedure and its algorithm content kind fits the leaf. Because RLT level conventions and the precise family of factor products vary, an authoritative source with a specific locator is required.

assumptions_latex: A bounded base system is written as nonnegative affine factors \(g_r(x)\ge0\).
Monomials through degree \(d+1\) receive consistent lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Linearized products of at most \(d+1\) nonnegative factors define a nested sequence of valid RLT relaxations.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative affine factors encoding constraints and bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: higher RLT levels linearize progressively higher-degree products of valid nonnegative factors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses degree of multiplied affine factors as the hierarchy-level convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the bounded base system as \(g_r(x)\ge0\). At level \(d\ge1\), generate
\[
\prod_{r}g_r(x)^{\alpha_r}\ge0
\qquad\text{for every }\alpha\in\mathbb Z_+^m
\text{ with }1\le\sum_r\alpha_r\le d+1,
\]
and apply \(\mathcal L_d\) to replace each monomial by its lifted coordinate. Include consistency equations whenever two products represent the same monomial, and project or optimize over the resulting linear system. With a common lifted-coordinate convention, the projected regions satisfy
\[
R_{d+1}\subseteq R_d,
\]
and every exact lifted feasible point belongs to every \(R_d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Higher RLT levels multiply more valid nonnegative affine factors, linearize the resulting higher-degree monomials, and form nested, progressively stronger relaxations.
knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Level RLT Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record explicitly declares its degree convention and states only validity and nesting, but the use of arbitrary repeated affine factors and the indexing of level d are convention-dependent. No authoritative source is supplied to establish this exact higher-level RLT variant.

children.title: Lift–Project Operators
children.top_down_role: Operators that construct stronger lifted polyhedral QCQP relaxations.

assumptions_latex: A convex relaxation \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) contains the target feasible set \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The operator \(T_D(R)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_k(R\cap D_k))\) preserves \(F\) and satisfies \(T_D(R)\subseteq R\).

notation.meaning: Lift-project operator associated with the disjunction

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: disjunctive lift-project operators convexify branchwise intersections and project
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a generic disjunctive lift-project operator applicable to a convex lifted QCQP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(R\) is convex, and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\) satisfy \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^qD_k\). The disjunctive lift-project operator is
\[
T_D(R)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^q(R\cap D_k)\right).
\]
An implementation may construct an extended formulation for the convex hull and then project it onto the original or QCQP-lifted coordinates. Validity of the disjunction and convexity of \(R\) give
\[
F\subseteq T_D(R)\subseteq R.
\]
Repeated application with selected disjunctions defines progressively strengthened relaxations, with output equal to the projected convexified union at each step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex relaxation, a lift-project operator intersects it with every branch of a valid disjunction, convexifies the union in lifted space, and projects back.
knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Project Operators

children.title: Disjunctive Lifted Cuts
children.top_down_role: Lifted inequalities derived from disjunctive structure.

assumptions_latex: Each branch is a nonempty bounded polyhedron \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\le b_k\}\).
The disjunction \(x\in\bigcup_{k=1}^qP_k\) is valid for the target feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted disjunctive formulation projects to \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_kP_k)\), and every inequality valid for that projection is a valid disjunctive cut.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: homogenized disjunctive formulation represents the convex hull of a finite union of nonempty bounded polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the bounded-polyhedral disjunctive hull formulation used to generate projected cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For nonempty bounded polyhedra \(P_k=\{x:A_kx\le b_k\}\), introduce \(x^k\) and \(\lambda_k\) satisfying
\[
x=\sum_{k=1}^qx^k,
\qquad A_kx^k\le b_k\lambda_k,
\qquad \lambda_k\ge0,
\qquad \sum_{k=1}^q\lambda_k=1.
\]
The projection of this lifted system onto \(x\) is exactly
\[
\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{k=1}^qP_k\right).
\]
Hence any inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) valid for that projection, and violated by the current relaxation point, is a disjunctive lifted cut. Its validity is checked against the displayed linear extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregated branch variables and convex weights represent the convex hull of a bounded polyhedral disjunction; inequalities valid for its projection are disjunctive cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Lifted Cuts

children.title: Projection Closure Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Successive closure levels obtained through repeated lifting or projection.

assumptions_latex: \(P^0\subseteq [0,1]^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\) is a convex relaxation containing every lifted feasible mixed-binary point.
Projection is onto the original variables and any retained lifted coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{t+1}\subseteq P^t\) and every lifted feasible mixed-binary point belongs to every \(P^t\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: recursive disjunctive projection closures are a standard lift-project construction
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive coordinate-disjunction closure for binary variables in a lifted QCQP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define the coordinate closure \[D_i(P)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x_i=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x_i=1\})\bigr).\] The projection-closure hierarchy generated from \(P^0\) is \[P^{t+1}=\bigcap_{i=1}^n D_i(P^t),\qquad t=0,1,\ldots .\] Since each disjunctive set is contained in \(P^t\), convexity gives \(D_i(P^t)\subseteq P^t\), hence \(P^{t+1}\subseteq P^t\). Every point of \(P^0\) whose binary coordinates lie in \(\{0,1\}^n\) survives every closure, so each level remains a valid relaxation of the lifted mixed-binary feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly convexify each binary-coordinate disjunction and intersect the results. The projected relaxations are nested and retain all feasible mixed-binary points.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Closure Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recurrence, nesting claim, and content kind are mathematically appropriate for the projection-closure leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied. The statement also includes a proof-style justification beginning with the disjunctive-set inclusion; that text should be removed when the record is resubmitted with a source.

children.title: Finite-Level Strength
children.top_down_role: Bound quality and formulation growth at finite hierarchy levels.

assumptions_latex: The hierarchy \((P^t)_{t\geq0}\) is generated by valid lift-project closures.
The relaxed objective is linear and is minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t\leq v_{t+1}\leq v_*\), where \(v_*\) is the mixed-binary optimum.

notation.meaning: Optimal relaxation value at level t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nesting and bound monotonicity follow directly from valid closure inclusion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-level dominance, without asserting finite exactness for an unspecified lift-project operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_I\subseteq P^t\) denote the lifted mixed-binary feasible set at every level, and let \(P^{t+1}\subseteq P^t\). For a linear objective \(c^{\mathsf T}z\), define \[v_t=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}z:z\in P^t\},\qquad v_* =\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}z:z\in F_I\}.\] Then set inclusion implies \[v_t\leq v_{t+1}\leq v_* .\] Thus every finite level is at least as strong as its predecessor for minimization, while remaining a valid lower-bounding relaxation. Equality between consecutive bounds need not imply that \(P^t\) equals the mixed-binary convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each finite closure level is contained in the previous one, so minimization bounds improve monotonically but need not yet be exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Level Strength

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonic lower-bound property is correct for nested valid minimization relaxations, and property is the right content kind. An authoritative locator is still required, and the set-inclusion derivation should be removed from the final knowledge statement.

assumptions_latex: The QCQP variables satisfy linear inequalities \(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r\geq0\).
The lift uses \(X\) to represent \(xx^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SDP-RLT feasible region contains every \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) feasible for the QCQP and is convex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order SDP relaxation intersected with linearized products of valid affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SDP-RLT relaxation replaces \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \[Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}\succeq0,\] expresses every quadratic constraint \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2q^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\geq0\) as \(\langle Q,X\rangle+2q^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\geq0\), and adds linearizations of valid products \[(a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r)(a_s^{\mathsf T}x-b_s)\geq0.\] The corresponding lifted inequality is \[a_r^{\mathsf T}Xa_s-b_s a_r^{\mathsf T}x-b_r a_s^{\mathsf T}x+b_rb_s\geq0.\] Their intersection is convex and contains every exact lift \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) of a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SDP-RLT combines a positive-semidefinite moment constraint, linearized quadratic constraints, and linearized products of valid affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: SDP-RLT Relaxations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and formulas are standard, but the cited sections on the SDP cone, LMIs, and SDP programming do not specifically support the RLT product constraints or the combined SDP-RLT construction. A dedicated RLT or SDP-RLT source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Valid Quadratic Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Valid quadratic restrictions used to strengthen QCQP relaxations.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the original QCQP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(q(x)\geq0\) on \(F\), then \(\langle Q,X\rangle+2d^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\geq0\) is valid for every exact lifted feasible point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and linearization of a quadratic inequality on the original feasible set.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.5, Convex Inequalities, p. 52

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic inequality \[q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2d^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\geq0\] is valid for \(F\) precisely when \(q(x)\geq0\) for every \(x\in F\). Under the exact lifting equation \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), one has \(x^{\mathsf T}Qx=\langle Q,X\rangle\). Consequently, every valid quadratic inequality induces the lifted affine inequality \[\langle Q,X\rangle+2d^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\geq0.\] This inequality remains valid for the lifted feasible set \(\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in F\}\) and may be imposed on a relaxation containing that set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic inequality is valid when it holds throughout the QCQP feasible set; lifting replaces each quadratic product by its corresponding matrix entry.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Quadratic Inequalities

source_witnesses.locator: Section 2.5, Convex Inequalities, p. 52

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition and lifted affine inequality are mathematically correct, and condition fits the leaf. The cited section on convex inequalities does not inspectably support quadratic lifting or the matrix linearization, so a more specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a multiplier-indexed family of valid inequalities for a QCQP and records that the aggregated inequalities need not themselves be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a QCQP with objective quadratic matrix \(Q_0\) and constraints \(q_k(x)=x^\top Q_kx+2b_k^\top x-a_k\le 0\), \(k=1,\ldots,m\). For any \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \(Q_0+\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kQ_k\succeq0\), the inequality \(\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kq_k(x)\le0\) is called a valid inequality for the QCQP. This generally gives an infinite family, and an aggregated inequality need not be convex because \(\sum_k\lambda_kQ_k\) need not be positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative aggregation of the quadratic constraints belongs to this valid-inequality family when its quadratic matrix, after addition to the objective matrix, is positive semidefinite. The family is generally infinite, and its inequalities need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_kq_k(x)\le0\text{ is a valid quadratic inequality; such inequalities form a generally infinite, not necessarily convex family.}

children.title: Valid Product Inequalities
children.top_down_role: Valid inequalities obtained from products of bounded or sign-restricted expressions.

assumptions_latex: The affine inequalities \(a(x)=a_0+a^{\mathsf T}x\geq0\) and \(b(x)=b_0+b^{\mathsf T}x\geq0\) are valid on \(F\).
The lift uses \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\) on exact points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The linearized product inequality is valid for every exact lift of \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multiplying two nonnegative affine functions gives the standard RLT product inequality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RLT product inequalities generated from pairs of nonnegative affine functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(a(x)\geq0\) and \(b(x)\geq0\) on \(F\), their product satisfies \(a(x)b(x)\geq0\) on \(F\). Expanding and replacing \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) by \(X\) gives \[\langle ab^{\mathsf T},X\rangle+a_0b^{\mathsf T}x+b_0a^{\mathsf T}x+a_0b_0\geq0.\] Since \(X\) is symmetric, \(ab^{\mathsf T}\) may equivalently be replaced by \((ab^{\mathsf T}+ba^{\mathsf T})/2\). At every exact lifted point \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\), the left-hand side equals \(a(x)b(x)\); hence the displayed affine inequality is valid for the exact lifted feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying two valid nonnegative affine inequalities yields a valid quadratic inequality whose lifted form is affine in the matrix variable.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Product Inequalities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The RLT product formula is correct and property is an appropriate content kind, but there is no cited source. The expansion and validity argument are proof text and should be replaced by a direct statement when sourced.

children.title: Lifted Inequality Representations
children.top_down_role: Conic or linear lifted representations of valid quadratic or product restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The homogenized lift satisfies \(Y=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\) on exact points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=\langle H,Y\rangle\) for exact lifts, while dropping \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\) produces an affine lifted inequality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous matrix representation of quadratic inequalities and their affine lift.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.14.2, Linear Matrix Inequality, p. 83

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2d^{\mathsf T}x+q_0\), define \[H=\begin{pmatrix}q_0&d^{\mathsf T}\\d&Q\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}1&x^{\mathsf T}\\x&X\end{pmatrix}.\] If \(X=xx^{\mathsf T}\), then \(Y=(1,x)(1,x)^{\mathsf T}\) and \[q(x)=\langle H,Y\rangle=\langle Q,X\rangle+2d^{\mathsf T}x+q_0.\] Hence \(q(x)\geq0\) is represented exactly by \(\langle H,Y\rangle\geq0\) together with \(Y\succeq0\), \(Y_{00}=1\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)=1\). Omitting the rank constraint yields its standard convex lifted representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization represents a quadratic inequality as a matrix inner product. Exactness requires a rank-one moment matrix; deleting rank gives a convex relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Inequality Representations

source_witnesses.locator: Section 2.14.2, Linear Matrix Inequality, p. 83

children.title: Joint Strengthening Effects
children.top_down_role: Relaxation improvements obtained by combining compatible valid-inequality families.

assumptions_latex: Each relaxation contains every exact lifted feasible point.
A common linear objective is minimized over all relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(R=R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\cap R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\cap R_{\mathrm{VQI}}\), one has \(v(R)\geq\max\{v(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}),v(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}),v(R_{\mathrm{VQI}})\}\).

notation.meaning: Minimum of the common objective over a region

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: intersection dominance and minimization-bound monotonicity are elementary set-inclusion consequences
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength obtained by intersecting complementary valid lifted inequality families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\), \(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\), and \(R_{\mathrm{VQI}}\) be valid lifted relaxations of the same feasible set, and define \[R=R_{\mathrm{SDP}}\cap R_{\mathrm{RLT}}\cap R_{\mathrm{VQI}}.\] Then \(R\) contains every exact lifted feasible point and satisfies \(R\subseteq R_j\) for each constituent region \(R_j\). For a common linear minimization objective, set \(v(S)=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}z:z\in S\}\). Set inclusion yields \[v(R)\geq\max\{v(R_{\mathrm{SDP}}),v(R_{\mathrm{RLT}}),v(R_{\mathrm{VQI}})\}.\] The inequality can be strict when different families exclude different relaxed points; strictness is not guaranteed for every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting SDP, RLT, and other valid lifted inequalities preserves validity and gives a minimization bound at least as strong as every constituent relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Strengthening Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Intersection dominance for a common minimization objective is correct, and property fits the terminal container. No source is supplied, and the set-inclusion derivation should be removed from the final sourced statement.

assumptions_latex: Distinct variables satisfy finite valid bounds \(\ell_i\leq x_i\leq u_i\) and \(\ell_j\leq x_j\leq u_j\), where \(i\neq j\).
The lifted variable \(X_{ij}\) represents \(x_i x_j\) at exact lifted points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(i\neq j\), every exact product satisfies the four McCormick inequalities, and these inequalities describe the convex hull of the bilinear graph over \([\ell_i,u_i]\times[\ell_j,u_j]\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower and upper bounds for variables i and j
Lifted surrogate for the bilinear product of two distinct variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: McCormick strengthening for a bounded bilinear term involving two distinct variables; diagonal square terms require separate treatment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(i\neq j\), with \(x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i]\), \(x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\), and \(X_{ij}=x_i x_j\) at exact lifted points. The McCormick inequalities are \[X_{ij}\geq \ell_i x_j+\ell_j x_i-\ell_i\ell_j,\qquad X_{ij}\geq u_i x_j+u_j x_i-u_i u_j,\] \[X_{ij}\leq u_i x_j+\ell_j x_i-u_i\ell_j,\qquad X_{ij}\leq \ell_i x_j+u_j x_i-\ell_i u_j.\] They are valid for every exact lifted point and describe the convex hull of \(\{(x_i,x_j,X_{ij}):X_{ij}=x_i x_j,\ x_i\in[\ell_i,u_i],\ x_j\in[\ell_j,u_j]\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two distinct bounded variables, the four McCormick inequalities validly strengthen the lifted bilinear term and give the exact convex hull of its graph over the bounds rectangle.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dependent Strengthening

children.title: Symmetry-Aware Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Relaxation strengthening based on invariant structure or orbit information.

assumptions_latex: A finite group \(G\) acts through orthogonal matrices \(P_g\).
The convex relaxation \(R\) and linear objective are invariant under \((x,X)\mapsto(P_gx,P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Averaging any feasible point over \(G\) gives an invariant feasible point with the same objective value.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-group averaging over an invariant convex set is the Reynolds-operator principle
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex symmetry reduction by averaging lifted feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \((x,X)\in R\), define the group average \[\mathcal{R}_G(x,X)=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}(P_gx,P_gXP_g^{\mathsf T}).\] Invariance makes every summand feasible, and convexity gives \(\mathcal{R}_G(x,X)\in R\). The average is fixed by every group element: for all \(h\in G\), \[P_h\bar x=\bar x,\qquad P_h\bar X P_h^{\mathsf T}=\bar X,\] where \((\bar x,\bar X)=\mathcal{R}_G(x,X)\). If the linear objective is group-invariant, its value at the average equals its value at \((x,X)\). Thus optimization may be restricted to the fixed-point subspace without changing the relaxation optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an invariant convex relaxation, averaging over the symmetry group produces an invariant feasible point with unchanged objective, permitting restriction to the fixed-point subspace.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Aware Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Finite-group averaging is mathematically standard, but the record describes an objective-preserving fixed-point reduction rather than relaxation strengthening that preserves every exact lifted feasible point. That subject is already aligned with the sibling Orbit-Based Reductions leaf, so it does not fit this exact terminal container. It also lacks a source.

children.title: Sparsity-Aware Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Relaxation strengthening localized to sparse interaction patterns.

assumptions_latex: The aggregate sparsity graph \(H=(V,E)\) is chordal.
All entries of a partial symmetric matrix are specified on the diagonal and edges of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A partial matrix has a positive-semidefinite completion exactly when every maximal-clique principal submatrix is positive semidefinite.

notation.meaning: Family of maximal cliques of H
Principal submatrix indexed by clique C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard chordal positive-semidefinite completion theorem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal PSD-completion form underlying sparse semidefinite QCQP relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(V,E)\) be chordal and let \(Y\) be a partial symmetric matrix whose specified entries are \(Y_{ii}\) for \(i\in V\) and \(Y_{ij}\) for \(\{i,j\}\in E\). Then \(Y\) admits a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \[Y[C]\succeq0\qquad\text{for every maximal clique }C\in\mathcal{C}(H).\] Shared entries of clique submatrices must represent the same partial-matrix variables. Consequently, a sparse lifted QCQP relaxation may replace one global PSD-completability condition by PSD constraints on maximal cliques, provided the chosen chordal extension contains every matrix entry used by the objective and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, a partial matrix has a PSD completion exactly when all maximal-clique principal submatrices are PSD and agree on overlaps.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Aware Strengthening

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The chordal PSD-completion theorem is stated correctly, with the necessary shared-entry consistency and support qualification, and theorem is the correct mathematical role. A precise authoritative source for the completion theorem is required.

children.title: Orbit-Based Reductions
children.top_down_role: Reduction of lifted variables or constraints through symmetry orbits.

assumptions_latex: A finite permutation group \(G\) acts linearly on the lifted variable \(z\), and the convex feasible region \(R\) is invariant under this action.
The linear objective is invariant under \(G\), and its minimum over \(R\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation has an optimal solution in \(\operatorname{Fix}(G)\), and the fixed-point variables can be parameterized by the coordinate orbits of the permutation action.

notation.meaning: Fixed-point subspace of the group action
Reynolds projector onto the fixed-point subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orbit-coordinate reduction for an attained invariant convex relaxation under a finite permutation group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite permutation group \(G\), define \[\Pi_G z=\frac{1}{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}gz,\qquad \operatorname{Fix}(G)=\{z:gz=z\text{ for every }g\in G\}.\] If \(R\) and the linear objective are invariant under \(G\), then \(\Pi_G z\in R\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)\) and has the same objective value as \(z\) for every \(z\in R\). If the minimum over \(R\) is attained, an optimal solution exists in \(R\cap\operatorname{Fix}(G)\). On this subspace, coordinates in the same permutation orbit are equal; symmetric-matrix coordinates are parameterized by unordered-pair orbits. One parameter per orbit therefore gives an equivalent reduced convex optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an attained invariant convex relaxation under a finite permutation group, averaging yields an optimal fixed point, and one variable per coordinate or matrix-entry orbit gives an equivalent reduced formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Orbit-Based Reductions

children.title: Clique-Localized Strengthening
children.top_down_role: Strengthening restrictions applied within sparse clique substructures.

assumptions_latex: A chordal extension has maximal-clique family \(\mathcal{C}\), and the base region \(R_{\mathrm{sparse}}\) contains every exact lift \((x,xx^{\mathsf T})\) of the original feasible set \(F\).
For every \(C\in\mathcal{C}\), each \(\ell\in\mathcal{L}_C\) is an affine function of \((x_C,X[C])\) satisfying \(\ell(x_C,x_Cx_C^{\mathsf T})\geq0\) for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The clique-strengthened region contains every exact lift of \(F\) and is contained in \(R_{\mathrm{sparse}}\).

notation.meaning: Maximal cliques of the chordal extension
Family of valid affine lifted inequalities supported on clique C

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid affine lifted cuts imposed on maximal-clique variables of a sparse semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(C\in\mathcal{C}\), let \(\mathcal{L}_C\) be a family of affine functions of \((x_C,X[C])\) that are nonnegative at every exact lift of \(F\). Define \[R_{\mathrm{clique}}=R_{\mathrm{sparse}}\cap\bigcap_{C\in\mathcal{C}}\bigcap_{\ell\in\mathcal{L}_C}\{(x,X):\ell(x_C,X[C])\geq0\}.\] Then \[\{(x,xx^{\mathsf T}):x\in F\}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{clique}}\subseteq R_{\mathrm{sparse}}.\] The families \(\mathcal{L}_C\) may include clique-supported RLT, bound-derived, or valid-quadratic inequalities, and they introduce no lifted matrix entries outside the corresponding clique supports.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting a sparse SDP relaxation with explicitly quantified valid inequalities supported on its cliques preserves every exact lift and produces a region contained in the base sparse relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Clique-Localized Strengthening

assumptions_latex: The QCQP variables satisfy \(x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), and all objective and constraint functions are quadratic.
The lifted feasible set is explicitly constrained to equal the convex hull of its feasible rank-one lifts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reformulation has the same infimum as the QCQP, and every rank-one feasible lift recovers a feasible QCQP point.

notation.meaning: Completely positive cone generated by nonnegative rank-one matrices.
Homogeneous lift of a QCQP point.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: completely positive lifting is the standard exact convexification of nonnegative rank-one quadratic lifts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonnegative QCQP lifting; exactness requires the stated convex-hull description.

source_refs.locator: 3.9 The GOP for Quadratically Constrained Problems p. 96

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write every quadratic function as \(q_i(x)=\langle Q_i,zz^\top\rangle\), where \(z=(1,x)\). If the convex hull of feasible lifted matrices is described by \[\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathcal{CP}^{n+1}:\langle H_j,X\rangle=b_j\ (j=1,\ldots,m),\ \langle E_{00},X\rangle=1\},\] then replacing \(X=zz^\top\) by \(X\in\mathcal F\) yields the conic program \[\inf\{\langle Q_0,X\rangle:X\in\mathcal F\}.\] Its value equals \(\inf\{q_0(x):x\text{ is QCQP-feasible}\}\); a rank-one optimum \(X=zz^\top\) with \(z_0=1\) recovers \(x=z_{1:n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative QCQP is exactly convexified by optimizing over the completely positive convex hull of its feasible rank-one lifts; rank-one optimal lifts directly recover optimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Completely Positive Reformulations

source_witnesses.locator: 3.9 The GOP for Quadratically Constrained Problems p. 96

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional convex-hull reformulation is mathematically coherent and the representation kind fits, but the cited GOP section does not clearly support the specific completely positive reformulation or recovery claim. A copositive-programming source with a theorem or page-level locator is required.

assumptions_latex: The homogenized variable lies in a closed cone \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\).
The stated affine slice of \(\mathcal{CP}(K)\) equals the closed convex hull of feasible rank-one lifts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generalized completely positive primal is exact, and its conic dual uses the generalized copositive cone \(\mathcal{COP}(K)\).

notation.meaning: Generalized completely positive cone over K.
Adjoint of the affine constraint map.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generalized copositive programming is conic duality between rank-one cones generated over K and quadratic forms nonnegative on K
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cone-homogeneous formulation; closure and convex-hull hypotheses are explicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed cone \(K\), the cones \(\mathcal{CP}(K)\) and \(\mathcal{COP}(K)\) are dual under the trace pairing: \[\mathcal{CP}(K)^*=\mathcal{COP}(K).\] Hence an exact lifted problem \[\inf\{\langle Q,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\in\mathcal{CP}(K)\}\] has the generalized copositive dual \[\sup\{b^\top y:Q-\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathcal{COP}(K)\}.\] Weak duality always holds. Equality of primal and dual values additionally requires an applicable conic strong-duality condition, such as strict feasibility of one side together with finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized completely positive lifting over a cone K is dual to requiring a quadratic form to be nonnegative on K; strong duality needs a regularity condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Copositive Reformulations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generalized completely positive/copositive duality statement is plausible and the duality kind fits, but no source is supplied for the cone definitions, dual formula, or strong-duality qualification.

assumptions_latex: A copositive dual maximization has slack \(Q-\mathcal A^*(y)\in\mathcal{COP}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restricted values are valid lower bounds and satisfy \(\beta_r\le\beta_{r+1}\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: Level-r tractable inner approximation of the generalized copositive cone.
Optimal value of the level-r restricted dual.
Optimal value of the primal minimization problem.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested inner approximations of a dual feasibility cone yield monotone valid bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner semidefinite or SOS approximations of a generalized copositive dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the tractable level-\(r\) dual bound by \[\beta_r=\sup\{b^\top y:Q-\mathcal A^*(y)\in C_r\}.\] Because \(C_r\subseteq\mathcal{COP}(K)\), every level-\(r\) feasible multiplier is feasible for the exact copositive dual; therefore \(\beta_r\le p^*\). Nestedness gives \(\beta_r\le\beta_{r+1}\). If \(\bigcup_r C_r\) is dense in the relevant copositive slacks and an optimal slack admits the required approximation without destroying feasibility, then \(\beta_r\to p^*\); finite convergence is not implied by nestedness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested tractable inner approximations of the copositive cone produce monotone valid lower bounds. Convergence requires density and stability; finite convergence is not automatic.
knowledge_statements.title: Tractable Copositive Approximations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Nested inner cones do yield monotone valid dual bounds, but the asserted convergence condition is informal and no source identifies the intended approximation hierarchy or its convergence theorem.

assumptions_latex: The QCQP is written as polynomial optimization \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):g_i(x)\ge0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), with all polynomials quadratic or lower.
The feasible set is compact and its quadratic module is Archimedean.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Moment and SOS relaxations are primal-dual descriptions of the same order, and their bounds increase to \(p^*\).

notation.meaning: Localizing matrix for constraint polynomial g_i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lasserre moment relaxations and truncated quadratic-module SOS certificates are standard primal-dual interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Archimedean polynomial formulation of a real QCQP.

source_refs.locator: 2.13.2 Generalized Convex Optimization p. 78

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At order \(r\ge1\), the moment relaxation minimizes \(L_y(f)\) subject to \(y_0=1\), \(M_r(y)\succeq0\), and \(M_{r-\lceil\deg(g_i)/2\rceil}(g_i y)\succeq0\) whenever defined. Its SOS dual maximizes \(\gamma\) subject to \[f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\qquad \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2r,\] where every \(\sigma_i\) is a sum of squares. Under SDP strong duality the two order-\(r\) values agree; under the Archimedean assumption these values converge monotonically to \(p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-r moment matrices and degree-2r SOS certificates form primal-dual QCQP bounds. Under an Archimedean compactness condition, their common bounds converge upward to the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Moment-SOS Hierarchy Interface

source_witnesses.locator: 2.13.2 Generalized Convex Optimization p. 78

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moment–SOS interface and content kind are standard, but the cited generalized-convex-optimization section does not specifically substantiate moment matrices, localizing matrices, truncated SOS duality, or Archimedean convergence.

children.title: Quadratic Bound Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Quadratic-order bounds within the higher-order relaxation boundary.

assumptions_latex: The QCQP is represented by inequalities \(g_i(x)\ge0\) and objective \(f(x)\), all of degree at most two.
A degree-two truncated quadratic-module certificate is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The largest certified \(\gamma\) is a valid lower bound on the QCQP optimum.
review_flags: terminology_ambiguous: quadratic bound hierarchy may denote a project-specific hierarchy rather than degree-two truncated certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpreted as total-degree-two nonnegativity certificates for a QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\beta_2=\sup\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sigma_0+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i g_i,\ \sigma_i\text{ sum of squares},\ \deg(\sigma_i g_i)\le2\right\}.\] For every feasible \(x\), each term \(\sigma_i(x)g_i(x)\) and \(\sigma_0(x)\) is nonnegative, so certificate feasibility entails \(f(x)\ge\gamma\). Consequently \(\beta_2\le p^*\). This level uses only Gram matrices needed for sum-of-squares polynomials whose products in the displayed identity have total degree at most two.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic-degree SOS identity certifies a global lower bound for the QCQP. Maximizing the certified constant defines the quadratic bound level.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Bound Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed degree-two SOS certificate gives a valid bound, but no evidence establishes that the taxonomy's “Quadratic Bound Hierarchy” denotes this particular truncated quadratic-module construction or that certificate is its intended terminal knowledge kind.

children.title: Cubic Bound Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Cubic-order bounds within the higher-order relaxation boundary.

assumptions_latex: The QCQP is represented by inequalities \(g_i(x)\ge0\) and objective \(f(x)\), all of degree at most two.
Products in the positivity certificate are restricted to total degree at most three.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The largest degree-three certified \(\gamma\) is a valid lower bound and cannot be weaker than the degree-two bound.

notation.meaning: Products of defining inequalities indexed by a subset I.

review_flags: terminology_ambiguous: odd-degree hierarchy levels depend on whether products, non-SOS multipliers, or reformulation-linearization constraints are intended
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpreted as a degree-three preordering certificate, allowing products of valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_\varnothing=1\). Define \[\beta_3=\sup\left\{\gamma:f-\gamma=\sum_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}}\sigma_I g_I,\ \sigma_I\text{ sum of squares},\ \deg(\sigma_I g_I)\le3\right\}.\] Every summand is nonnegative on the feasible set, hence \(\beta_3\le p^*\). Since every degree-two certificate remains admissible at degree three, \(\beta_2\le\beta_3\). Odd total degree can arise through multiplication of a quadratic or constant SOS multiplier by linear defining inequalities; an SOS polynomial itself still has even degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degree-three certificates add products of valid inequalities while retaining SOS multipliers. They yield valid lower bounds at least as strong as the quadratic level.
knowledge_statements.title: Cubic Bound Hierarchy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The degree-three preordering certificate is conditionally valid, including its use of linear defining inequalities to obtain odd total degree, but no source establishes that this is the intended cubic hierarchy or terminal knowledge kind.

children.title: Cross-Order Bound Comparison
children.top_down_role: Relative strength, cost, nesting, and separation between the two hierarchy orders.

assumptions_latex: For each integer \(d\ge2\), the degree-d certificate cone is contained in the degree-\((d+1)\) cone.
Every feasible certificate proves \(f(x)\ge\gamma\) on the QCQP feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hierarchy satisfies \(\beta_d\le\beta_{d+1}\le p^*\), but strict improvement and finite convergence need not occur.

notation.meaning: Best lower bound certified at total degree d.
Feasible certificate set at degree d.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested valid certificate cones imply monotone bounds by feasible-set inclusion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison by nested certificate degree, independent of whether convergence is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta_d=\sup\{\gamma:(f-\gamma,\gamma)\text{ admits a certificate in }\mathcal C_d\}\). If \(\mathcal C_d\subseteq\mathcal C_{d+1}\), feasible-set inclusion gives \(\beta_d\le\beta_{d+1}\). Certificate validity gives \(\beta_{d+1}\le p^*\). Thus, in particular, \[\beta_2\le\beta_3\le p^*.\] Equality \(\beta_d=\beta_{d+1}\) is possible, so increasing order need not improve a particular instance. Moreover, monotonicity alone implies neither convergence to \(p^*\) nor attainment of \(p^*\) at a finite order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested certificate orders give nondecreasing lower bounds bounded by the QCQP optimum. Consecutive levels may coincide, and monotonicity alone does not ensure convergence or finite exactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Order Bound Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity property follows from the stated nesting, and property fits the comparison container, but the underlying certificate cones and their cross-order nesting have no cited source.

Its relaxation has optimal value \(p_R^*\) under the same minimization convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization QCQP with value \[p^*=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\] and a relaxation with value \[p_R^*=\inf_{X\in R}\langle Q,X\rangle,\] where every feasible QCQP point has a feasible lift of the same objective value. The relaxation is objective-value exact if and only if \(p_R^*=p^*\). This definition concerns equality of infima only: it does not require either problem to attain its infimum, nor does it require an optimal relaxed solution to encode or recover a QCQP optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation is objective-value exact when its optimal value equals the QCQP optimal value. This alone neither guarantees attainment nor enables recovery of an optimizer.

assumptions_latex: The QCQP and its relaxation attain their optimal values.
A specified recovery map \(\rho\) is defined on relevant relaxed optima.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Optimizer-recovery exactness holds when some relaxed optimum recovers a QCQP optimum; universal recovery requires this for every relaxed optimum.

notation.meaning: Recovery map from lifted solutions to original variables.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: optimizer recovery is defined by mapping optimal relaxed solutions to optimal original solutions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential recovery is distinguished from universal recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in F}f(x)\) and let \(R^*\) be the relaxed optimal set. The relaxation is optimizer-recovery exact relative to \(\rho\) if \[\rho(R^*)\cap F^*\ne\varnothing.\] It is universally optimizer-recovery exact if \[\rho(X)\in F^*\qquad\text{for every }X\in R^*.\] Either property implies objective-value exactness when the recovery map preserves the objective value. Objective-value exactness by itself does not imply optimizer recovery, because a relaxed optimum may have no admissible rank-one representation or recoverable original point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery exactness means a specified map sends at least one relaxed optimum to a QCQP optimum; universal recovery requires this for every relaxed optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Slack Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corank-one dual-slack certificate for rank-one recovery from a standard-form SDP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ X\succeq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:Z=C-\sum_i y_iA_i\succeq0\}\). If primal-feasible \(X\) and dual-feasible \((y,Z)\) satisfy \(\langle C,X\rangle=b^{\mathsf T}y\), then \(\langle Z,X\rangle=0\). Consequently \(XZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\ker Z\). If additionally \(X\neq0\) and \(\dim\ker Z=1\), then \(\operatorname{rank}X=1\); hence a normalized lifted QCQP relaxation admits recovery of its generating vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching primal and dual objectives plus a positive-semidefinite slack of nullity one certifies that the nonzero primal lift has rank one.

knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix complementarity certificate for optimality and recovery in primal-dual SDP pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the displayed primal-dual SDP pair, let \(X\succeq0\) and \(Z\succeq0\) be primal and dual feasible. The duality gap equals \(\langle Z,X\rangle\). Thus \(\langle Z,X\rangle=0\) certifies equality of the primal and dual objective values and therefore optimality of both feasible points. For positive-semidefinite matrices, \(\langle Z,X\rangle=0\) is equivalent to \(X^{1/2}ZX^{1/2}=0\), and hence to \(ZX=XZ=0\). It follows that \(\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq\ker Z\) and \(\operatorname{rank}X\leq\dim\ker Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero trace product of feasible positive-semidefinite primal and dual-slack matrices certifies optimality and bounds primal rank by slack nullity.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Certificate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp limitation of dual-slack complementarity when the slack kernel is not one-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Complementarity alone guarantees only \(\operatorname{rank}X\leq\dim\ker Z\). In particular, for \(n\geq3\), take \(Z=\operatorname{diag}(0,0,1,\ldots,1)\) and \(X=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,0,\ldots,0)\). Then \(X\succeq0\), \(Z\succeq0\), and \(XZ=0\), but \(\operatorname{rank}X=2\). Therefore a complementary primal-dual pair with \(\dim\ker Z\geq2\) does not by itself certify rank-one recovery. The certificate also fails if primal or dual feasibility is absent, or if the alleged slack is not positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complementarity with a multidimensional slack kernel permits higher-rank primal solutions, so it cannot alone certify rank-one recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Barvinok-Pataki Rank Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real-symmetric extreme-point rank bound for equality-form semidefinite programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F=\{X\in\mathbb S_+^n:\langle A_i,X\rangle=b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), where the affine equations are linearly independent. Every extreme point \(X\) of \(\mathcal F\), with \(r=\operatorname{rank}X\), satisfies \[\frac{r(r+1)}2\leq m.\] Consequently, if \(\mathcal F\) is nonempty and compact, then every linear objective over \(\mathcal F\) has an optimal solution whose rank obeys this bound. For an inequality-form SDP, the analogous bound uses the number of linearly independent constraints active on the relevant minimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extreme feasible SDP matrix has rank r satisfying r(r+1)/2 no greater than the number of independent active affine constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constructive Rank Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility- and objective-preserving rank reduction for a factored SDP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible \(X=VV^{\mathsf T}\) of rank \(r\), and set \(B_0=C\), \(B_i=A_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). If \(r(r+1)/2>m+1\), find nonzero \(H\in\mathbb S^r\) satisfying \(\langle V^{\mathsf T}B_iV,H\rangle=0\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\). Choose a nonzero boundary point \(t_*\) of \(\{t:I_r+tH\succeq0\}\), and update \(X\leftarrow V(I_r+t_*H)V^{\mathsf T}\). The update preserves all constraints and the objective while strictly decreasing rank. Refactor and repeat until no such \(H\) exists; output the final matrix.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(\widehat X\) is feasible, has the same objective value, and satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}\widehat X<\operatorname{rank}X\) after each update.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Rank Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine constraints can force every feasible SDP lift to have rank greater than one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any \(n\geq2\), consider the feasibility SDP requiring \(X\succeq0\), \(X_{jj}=1\) for every \(j\), and \(X_{jk}=0\) for every \(j<k\). Its unique feasible point is \(X=I_n\), which has rank \(n\). Equivalently, a zero linear objective makes \(I_n\) the unique optimum. Thus neither positive-semidefinite feasibility nor optimality ensures a rank-one solution: sufficiently many independent affine measurements can expose a singleton high-rank face, precluding rank-one recovery by any method that must preserve all measurements.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Constraint Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: S-lemma exactness for a QCQP with one quadratic inequality under strict feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2c_i^{\mathsf T}x+d_i\) for \(i=0,1\), and consider \(p^*=\inf\{q_0(x):q_1(x)\leq0\}\). If the QCQP attains its infimum at \(x^*\), then \([1;(x^*)][1;(x^*)]^{\mathsf T}\) is a rank-one optimal relaxation matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Structure Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank-one recovery for homogeneous QCQPs whose data matrices are diagonal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a homogeneous QCQP whose objective and every equality or inequality constraint are \(x^{\mathsf T}D_ix\), with each \(D_i\) diagonal. Since \(D_i\) is diagonal, \(x^{\mathsf T}D_ix=\sum_j(D_i)_{jj}z_j=\langle D_i,X\rangle\) for every \(i\). Hence \(xx^{\mathsf T}\) preserves every constraint and the objective, so the relaxation is exact whenever either problem attains its optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable-Structure Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise exactness composes for Cartesian-product QCQPs with block-local data.

If every block Shor relaxation is exact and attains a rank-one optimum generated by \(x_*^{(k)}\), then \(x_*=(x_*^{(1)},\ldots,x_*^{(p)})\) is globally optimal. Its full lift \([1;x_*][1;x_*]^{\mathsf T}\) is feasible and rank one, so the product problem's Shor relaxation is exact.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A three-cycle of cross-variable couplings destroys separability and creates an SDP gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{x_1x_2+x_2x_3+x_3x_1:x_i^2=1,\ i=1,2,3\}\). Every feasible sign vector has objective at least \(-1\), and this value is attained. knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Diagonalization Exactness

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Pattern Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connected signed saturation certificate for rank-one optimality of a Shor matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y\succeq0\) be an optimal Shor matrix indexed by \(0,1,\ldots,n\), with \(Y_{00}=1\) and \(Y_{ii}>0\). Suppose a connected spanning graph \(G\) and signs \(\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}\) satisfy \(Y_{ij}=\varepsilon_i\varepsilon_j\sqrt{Y_{ii}Y_{jj}}\) on every edge \(ij\in G\). In a Gram representation, equality in Cauchy-Schwarz makes the endpoint vectors signed-collinear. Connectivity makes all Gram vectors collinear, hence \(\operatorname{rank}Y=1\). Therefore \(x_j=Y_{0j}\) recovers a QCQP-feasible point with the relaxation objective, certifying exactness.

children.title: Symmetry-Induced Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness regimes supported by invariance or orbit structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Induced Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An invariant optimal-face criterion for exact recovery under a finite symmetry group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(\Gamma\) act orthogonally on \(\mathbb R^n\), preserving every lifted QCQP constraint and its objective. For any relaxed optimum \(X\), the Reynolds average \(\bar X=|\Gamma|^{-1}\sum_{g\in\Gamma}gXg^\top\) is invariant and optimal. Symmetry-induced exactness holds if the invariant part of the optimal face contains a feasible matrix \(X^\star\) of rank one. Writing \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\), the lifted equalities recover a feasible QCQP point with the relaxation value, hence zero relaxation gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetry-preserving SDP is exact when its invariant optimal face contains a rank-one matrix satisfying the lifted constraints.
assumptions_latex: The objective and feasible lifted set are \(\Gamma\)-invariant.
The invariant optimal face contains a feasible rank-one matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\) recovers a globally optimal QCQP point.

notation.meaning: Reynolds average of a lifted solution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is a valid sufficient rank-one recovery criterion and fits the container, but the specialized symmetry-exactness claim has no citation.

children.title: Eigenvalue-Multiplicity Exactness
children.top_down_role: Exactness regimes supported by repeated eigenvalues or enlarged eigenspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Multiplicity Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-slack nullity-one certificate for rank-one semidefinite relaxation exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X^\star\succeq0\) and \(S^\star\succeq0\) be primal and dual optimal matrices for a QCQP semidefinite relaxation, with zero duality gap and complementary slackness \(S^\star X^\star=0\). If the eigenvalue zero of \(S^\star\) has multiplicity one and the relaxation normalization excludes \(X^\star=0\), then \(\operatorname{range}(X^\star)\subseteq\ker S^\star\) implies \(\operatorname{rank}(X^\star)=1\). Factoring \(X^\star=x^\star(x^\star)^\top\) therefore supplies an exact QCQP optimizer whenever the lifted constraints faithfully encode feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero primal optimum is rank one when complementary slackness places its range in the one-dimensional kernel of the dual slack.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual optima exist with zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(X^\star)=1\), yielding exact recovery.

children.title: Symmetry-Breaking Boundary
children.top_down_role: Perturbations and asymmetries that remove the relevant structural advantage.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Breaking Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which symmetry no longer guarantees an invariant rank-one optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be the optimal face of a symmetry-invariant semidefinite relaxation and suppose \(F_0\) contains an invariant rank-one matrix. For perturbed data indexed by \(\varepsilon\), let \(F_\varepsilon\) denote the new optimal face. The symmetry-based exactness argument ceases to apply at the first parameter value for which either the perturbation is not invariant under the group action or \(F_\varepsilon\) has no rank-one member. Beyond this boundary, group averaging need not preserve the perturbed objective, and an invariant optimizer need not exist or yield QCQP recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetry-based recovery loses its guarantee once perturbations break invariance or remove every rank-one point from the relaxed optimal face.
assumptions_latex: \(F_\varepsilon\) is the perturbed relaxed optimal face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_\varepsilon\cap\{X:\operatorname{rank}(X)=1\}=\varnothing\) or broken invariance invalidates symmetry-induced exactness.

notation.meaning: optimal face under perturbation parameter epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits, but “the first parameter value” is undefined without an ordered parameter domain and perturbation path. A specialized source is also required to determine the intended rigorous formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Local-to-Global Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordal rank-one gluing criterion for sparse lifted QCQP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a chordal sparsity graph with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_m\), and suppose every coefficient appearing in the lifted QCQP objective and constraints is supported on a clique and is assigned consistently in the clique decomposition. Let \(X_{C_k}\succeq0\) be rank-one clique matrices satisfying the assigned local constraints and agreeing on every clique intersection. If rank-one factors of these matrices can be signed consistently along a clique tree, then there exists \(x\in\mathbb R^{|V|}\) such that \(X_{C_k}=x_{C_k}x_{C_k}^{\top}\) for every \(k\). Hence \(xx^{\top}\) is a global positive-semidefinite completion reproducing all represented objective and constraint values. If the clique matrices attain the sparse relaxation optimum, then \(x\) is feasible and globally optimal for the QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a chordal clique decomposition represents every objective and constraint term, consistently signed rank-one clique optima assemble into a globally optimal rank-one QCQP solution.
assumptions_latex: Every lifted objective and constraint coefficient is supported on and consistently assigned to the cliques.
The matrices \(X_{C_k}\) are positive semidefinite, rank one, locally feasible, and consistent on clique intersections.
Their rank-one factors admit consistent signs along a clique tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(x\in\mathbb R^{|V|}\) with \(X_{C_k}=x_{C_k}x_{C_k}^{\top}\) for all \(k\); if the clique matrices are relaxation-optimal, then \(x\) is globally QCQP-optimal.

notation.meaning: maximal clique of the chordal graph

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic leading-eigenvector recovery from an inexact lifted solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X\succeq0\), a domain-specific rounding map \(R\), and a prescribed constraint-violation merit function \(V\). Compute a unit eigenvector \(u_1\) associated with the largest eigenvalue \(\lambda_1(X)\), and set \(z=\sqrt{\lambda_1(X)}u_1\). Form every admissible candidate among \(R(z)\) and \(R(-z)\). If at least one candidate is feasible, output a feasible candidate having the smallest objective value. Otherwise output a candidate minimizing \(V\) for subsequent feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round both admissible signs of the dominant eigenvector and return the best feasible candidate, or the candidate with least prescribed constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: Objective values and feasibility can be evaluated for rounded candidates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the best feasible spectral candidate, or, if none is feasible, a candidate minimizing \(V\) among those generated.

notation.meaning: largest eigenvalue of the relaxed matrix

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian sampling and selection from a positive-semidefinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(X\in\mathbb S_+^n\), a factor \(L\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(LL^{\top}=X\), a rounding map \(R\), a prescribed constraint-violation merit function \(V\), and a sample count \(N\in\mathbb N\) with \(N\ge1\). For \(t=1,\ldots,N\), independently draw \(g_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_r)\), form \(z_t=Lg_t\), and set \(x_t=R(z_t)\). Output a feasible \(x_t\) of smallest objective value. If no candidate is feasible, output a candidate minimizing \(V\) for subsequent restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw N Gaussian vectors whose transformed covariance is the relaxed matrix, round them, and retain the best feasible or least-violating candidate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output belongs to \(\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\) and is selected by feasibility and objective value, or by \(V\) when no sample is feasible.

notation.meaning: number of columns of the factor L

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Restoration after Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation-minimization phase converting a rounded point into a tolerance-feasible QCQP point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) be finite index sets for constraints \(q_i(x)\le0\) and \(h_j(x)=0\), respectively. Input a rounded point \(x^{(0)}\), weights \(w_i>0\) and \(v_j>0\), inequality tolerances \(\eta_i\ge0\), and equality tolerances \(\xi_j\ge0\). Starting from \(x^{(0)}\), approximately minimize \(\Phi(x)=\sum_{i\in I}w_i[\max\{q_i(x),0\}]^2+\sum_{j\in J}v_jh_j(x)^2\), optionally subject to simple domain constraints. Stop when all prescribed feasibility tests hold, a stationary point is reached, or an iteration limit is met. Declare restoration successful exactly when \(q_i(x)\le\eta_i\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(|h_j(x)|\le\xi_j\) for every \(j\in J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize weighted constraint violation from the rounded point and declare success only after every inequality and equality meets its own prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restoration succeeds exactly when \(q_i(x)\le\eta_i\) for all \(i\in I\) and \(|h_j(x)|\le\xi_j\) for all \(j\in J\).

notation.meaning: inequality and equality constraint index sets

knowledge_statements.title: Local Polishing from Relaxation Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local constrained optimization initialized by a recovered relaxation candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a feasible or restored point \(x^{(0)}\) obtained from the relaxation and a local QCQP solver. Generate iterates by a descent globalization method, such as a trust-region or line-search sequential quadratic programming step, while enforcing or restoring constraint feasibility. Stop when the chosen first-order stationarity residual and constraint violation are below prescribed tolerances, or when an iteration limit is reached. Output the best feasible iterate encountered. For minimization, accept the polished point only if its objective does not exceed that of \(x^{(0)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start a local constrained solver from the recovered point and retain a feasible stationary iterate only when it improves the objective.
assumptions_latex: The initial point is feasible or supplied with a restoration mechanism.
Objective and constraint derivatives required by the local solver exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^{\mathrm{pol}})\le f(x^{(0)})\) whenever the polished point is accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict separation between the QCQP optimum and its relaxation or dual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization QCQP, let \(p^\star\) be its optimal value and let \(d^\star\) be the optimal value of a valid Lagrangian or semidefinite dual, so weak duality gives \(d^\star\le p^\star\). A positive duality gap occurs when both values are finite and \(p^\star-d^\star>0\). In that case the dual bound cannot certify global optimality of any feasible point having value \(p^\star\) by equality of bounds, and any primal relaxation sharing value \(d^\star\) is necessarily inexact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive difference between the QCQP optimum and its dual bound prevents equality-based optimality certification and signals relaxation failure.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual optimal values are finite.
The dual is valid, hence \(d^\star\le p^\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star-d^\star>0\) precludes a zero-gap certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Rank Optimal Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one recovery fails when the relaxed optimal face contains only higher-rank matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F^\star=\{X:X\text{ is feasible for the semidefinite relaxation and attains its optimal value}\}\). If \(F^\star\ne\varnothing\) and every \(X\in F^\star\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\ge2\), then direct rank-one factorization cannot recover a QCQP point attaining the relaxation value. Moreover, if every feasible QCQP point lifts to a rank-one matrix, the absence of rank-one matrices from \(F^\star\) proves that the relaxation is not exact in the solution-recovery sense, even when its optimal value happens to equal the QCQP value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every relaxed optimum has rank at least two, no optimal matrix can be factored directly into an exact QCQP solution.
assumptions_latex: The relaxed optimal face \(F^\star\) is nonempty.
Every QCQP point has a rank-one lift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F^\star\cap\{xx^\top:x\in\mathbb R^n\}=\varnothing\), so direct exact recovery fails.

notation.meaning: optimal face of the semidefinite relaxation
