knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of a minimization QCQP, and let \(R\) be a convex lifted relaxation in variables \((x,X)\) satisfying \((x,xx^\top)\in R\) for every \(x\in F\). The relaxation is weak after projection when \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\subsetneq\pi_x(R)\). Consequently, projected points can satisfy every constraint visible in \(\pi_x(R)\) without belonging to \(\operatorname{conv}(F)\). For a lifted objective \(\widehat f_0\) agreeing with \(f_0\) on \(X=xx^\top\), this weakness can manifest as \(\inf_{(x,X)\in R}\widehat f_0(x,X)<\inf_{x\in F}f_0(x)\); projection alone then cannot certify exactness or recover a feasible optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted convex relaxation is weakly projected when its original-variable projection strictly exceeds the convex hull of feasible QCQP points, potentially producing a strict lower-bound gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhibits infeasibility caused by first-moment extraction from a feasible semidefinite relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the quadratic feasibility set \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1^2+x_2^2=1\}\) and its lifted relaxation \(R=\{(x,X):X\succeq xx^\top,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=1\}\). The point \((0,\tfrac12 I_2)\) belongs to \(R\), since \(\tfrac12 I_2\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(\tfrac12 I_2)=1\). Under first-moment rounding \(\rho(x,X)=x\), however, its image is \(\rho(0,\tfrac12 I_2)=0\), which violates \(x_1^2+x_2^2=1\). Thus lifted feasibility does not imply feasibility of a rounded point unless the rounding rule preserves the original quadratic constraints or is followed by a valid repair step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible SDP point may round to an infeasible QCQP point; first-moment extraction maps a relaxed unit-circle point to the excluded origin.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in F\}\) be a minimization QCQP. Suppose a lifting maps every \(x\in F\) to \(z(x)\in R\), where \(R\) is defined by affine constraints and membership in a closed convex cone, and suppose \(\langle c,z(x)\rangle=f_0(x)\). Then the conic value \(L_R=\inf_{z\in R}\langle c,z\rangle\) satisfies \(L_R\le p^*\). If two valid conic relaxations satisfy \(R_1\subseteq R_2\), then \(L_{R_1}\ge L_{R_2}\). Hence adding valid conic constraints can only strengthen the lower bound, although equality with \(p^*\) additionally requires exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizing over any conic superset of the lifted feasible QCQP points gives a valid lower bound; a smaller valid relaxation gives a no-weaker bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-Envelope Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses product envelopes over bounded domains to obtain linear-programming lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in F\subseteq[\ell,u]\}\) be a bounded-domain minimization QCQP. Replace each off-diagonal bilinear term \(x_i x_j\), where \(i\ne j\), by \(w_{ij}\) and impose the McCormick inequalities \(w_{ij}\ge \ell_i x_j+\ell_j x_i-\ell_i\ell_j\), \(w_{ij}\ge u_i x_j+u_j x_i-u_i u_j\), \(w_{ij}\le u_i x_j+\ell_j x_i-u_i\ell_j\), and \(w_{ij}\le \ell_i x_j+u_j x_i-\ell_i u_j\). Let \(P\) combine these and any other valid polyhedral envelopes with relaxed QCQP constraints, and suppose every exact lifted point \((x,(x_i x_j)_{ij})\), for \(x\in F\), belongs to \(P\). If \(\widehat f_0(x,w)=f_0(x)\) at every exact lifted point, then \(L_P=\inf_{(x,w)\in P}\widehat f_0(x,w)\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid polyhedral product envelopes, including the McCormick envelope for bounded bilinear terms, contain every exact lifted feasible point. Minimizing the matching lifted objective over that outer approximation therefore gives a valid QCQP lower bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization QCQP \(p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f_0(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i g_i(x)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)\). For every primal-feasible \(x\) and every \(\lambda\ge0\), one has \(L(x,\lambda)\le f_0(x)\); hence \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\). The optimized Lagrangian bound \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\) therefore satisfies \(d^*\le p^*\). Equality is not guaranteed for a nonconvex QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative multipliers move inequality constraints into the objective. The supremum of the resulting infima is a valid lower bound, but nonconvexity may create a duality gap.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition the QCQP constraint indices into disjoint sets \(I\) and \(J\). Retain \(g_i(x)\le0\) explicitly for \(i\in I\), and dualize only \(g_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J\). The semi-Lagrangian function is \(q_J(\lambda_J)=\inf\{f_0(x)+\sum_{j\in J}\lambda_jg_j(x):x\in X,\ g_i(x)\le0\text{ for }i\in I\}\), where \(\lambda_J\ge0\). Every primal-feasible point is admissible in this infimum and has penalized value at most its objective value. Thus \(d_J=\sup_{\lambda_J\ge0}q_J(\lambda_J)\le p^*\). Retaining constraints may make the inner problem harder while strengthening its fixed-multiplier infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semi-Lagrangian bound dualizes only selected inequalities and enforces the rest explicitly, preserving lower-bound validity while trading inner-problem difficulty against relaxation strength.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_a\) and \(R_b\) be valid relaxation regions for the same lifted minimization QCQP, evaluated with the same objective \(\widehat f_0\). If \(R_a\subseteq R_b\), then \(L_a=\inf_{z\in R_a}\widehat f_0(z)\ge\inf_{z\in R_b}\widehat f_0(z)=L_b\); thus bound \(a\) dominates bound \(b\). Strict dominance occurs when \(L_a>L_b\). Without set inclusion, dominance may still hold for a particular objective, but it cannot be inferred solely from feasibility of both relaxations. Consequently, comparisons among Lagrangian, semi-Lagrangian, conic, and polyhedral bounds require a common formulation or an explicit value inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the same lifted minimization objective, a smaller valid relaxation gives a dominating lower bound. Without inclusion, dominance must be established by comparing bound values directly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization QCQP \(p^*=\inf\{f_0(x):x\in F\}\), any point \(\bar x\in F\) certifies the upper bound \(U=f_0(\bar x)\), because \(p^*\le f_0(\bar x)\). Verification consists of checking every original constraint at \(\bar x\) and evaluating \(f_0(\bar x)\); feasibility only in a relaxation is insufficient. Among feasible incumbents, replacing \(U\) by \(\min\{U,f_0(\bar x)\}\) preserves validity and improves the bound. If a global lower bound \(L\) is also available and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\), then \(\bar x\) is globally \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in absolute objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any point satisfying the original QCQP constraints gives an upper bound through its objective value. Together with a lower bound, it also certifies a global optimality gap.

Compute a valid node relaxation bound on each child, discard any child proved infeasible or fathomed by the incumbent, and otherwise add it to the active list. The children cover \(D\), and their interiors are disjoint. Repeated branching is exhaustive when the maximum width of boxes along every infinite branch tends to zero. A longest-edge or comparable rule that forces the maximum side length to zero along every infinite nested sequence yields an exhaustive rectangular partition. Terminate when no active rectangle can improve the incumbent beyond tolerance.

children.title: Partition Geometry Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Coverage, relaxation strength, refinement cost, and dimensional sensitivity across partition geometries.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition Geometry Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares partition shapes through relaxation accuracy and representation cost under a diameter-based error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact, and let \(\{P_j\}_{j=1}^k\) be a finite partition of \(P\). For each cell \(S\), let \(\gamma(S)\ge 0\) denote its worst-case relaxation gap, and suppose \(\gamma(S)\le C\operatorname{diam}(S)^2\) for a constant \(C\ge 0\). Defining the aggregate partition gap by \(G=\max_{1\le j\le k}\gamma(P_j)\), one has \(G\le C\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{diam}(P_j)^2\). Thus, under this error model, reducing the largest child diameter strengthens the worst-case bound. Axis-aligned rectangular cells preserve coordinate-bound descriptions, whereas simplicial cells permit oblique facets; selecting a geometry therefore trades directional alignment against the number and complexity of cells and inequalities required by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a quadratic diameter error bound, the worst child relaxation gap is controlled by the largest child diameter. Rectangles preserve coordinate bounds, while simplices permit oblique facets, so partition choice trades directional alignment against representation cost.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact and \(\{P_j\}_{j=1}^k\) is a finite partition of \(P\).
For every partition cell \(S\), \(0\le\gamma(S)\le C\operatorname{diam}(S)^2\) with \(C\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=\max_{1\le j\le k}\gamma(P_j)\le C\max_{1\le j\le k}\operatorname{diam}(P_j)^2\), with partition geometry also affecting representation cost.

notation.meaning: worst-case relaxation gap on cell S
maximum relaxation gap among the child cells

children.title: Spectral Branching Criteria
children.top_down_role: Branch selection based on spectral violations, gaps, or residual structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Branching Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a curvature-width score for selecting a spectral branching direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a symmetric curvature matrix \(H\), a compact node domain \(P\), and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), compute eigenpairs \((\lambda_i,v_i)\) with \(\|v_i\|_2=1\). Define the directional width \(w_i=\max_{x\in P}v_i^Tx-\min_{x\in P}v_i^Tx\) and score \(s_i=(-\lambda_i)_+w_i^2\). If \(\max_i s_i\le\tau\), spectral branching is not triggered. Otherwise select any \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i s_i\) and branch by partitioning the interval of \(v_{i^*}^Tx\). The score prioritizes directions combining negative curvature with substantial remaining domain width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the eigenvector whose negative curvature times squared domain width is largest, and branch on its projected coordinate unless the score is negligible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i(-\lambda_i)_+w_i^2\) is the selected spectral direction when its score exceeds \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: symmetric curvature matrix used by the branching rule
width of the node domain along eigenvector i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The curvature-width score is a plausible algorithmic heuristic, but no source establishes this exact score, trigger, or the curvature matrix used for a QCQP.

children.title: Eigenvector Branching Directions
children.top_down_role: Spatial disjunctions aligned with selected eigenvector directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvector Branching Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branches a node through a hyperplane orthogonal to a selected curvature eigenvector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a unit eigenvector of a symmetric curvature matrix associated with a negative eigenvalue. Compute \(a=\min_{x\in P}v^Tx\) and \(b=\max_{x\in P}v^Tx\). Choose \(t\in(a,b)\), commonly \(t=(a+b)/2\), and create children \(P^-=P\cap\{x:v^Tx\le t\}\) and \(P^+=P\cap\{x:v^Tx\ge t\}\). Their union is \(P\), and each child has a strictly smaller projected interval along \(v\). Repeated branching therefore localizes the coordinate carrying the selected negative-curvature contribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the node at an interior value of its projection onto a negative-curvature eigenvector, reducing uncertainty in that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P=P^-\cup P^+\), and both children have projected width strictly below \(b-a\).

notation.meaning: projection interval of the node along v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The split and projected-width reduction are mathematically sound, but evidence is required that this eigenvector-based procedure is an established spectral branching algorithm in the stated QCQP context.

children.title: Degenerate-Spectrum Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Multiplicity, clustering, and instability that weaken spectral branching choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Spectrum Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies nonuniqueness of eigenvector branching when the selected eigenvalue is repeated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a symmetric matrix \(H\) has a selected eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of multiplicity greater than one, an individual eigenvector is not invariantly determined. For example, when \(H=-I_2\), every unit vector in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) is an eigenvector with eigenvalue \(-1\), so an eigenvector-only branching rule can return arbitrarily rotated splits under infinitesimal perturbations or different eigensolvers. The invariant object is the eigenspace \(E=\ker(H-\lambda I)\), equivalently its orthogonal projector. A well-defined rule must add a basis-invariant secondary criterion over \(E\), such as maximizing node width.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated eigenvalues make individual eigenvectors nonunique; stable branching must select within the invariant eigenspace using an additional basis-independent criterion.
assumptions_latex: The selected eigenvalue \(\lambda\) has multiplicity greater than one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An eigenvalue alone does not determine a unique branching direction; selection must be formulated over \(E=\ker(H-\lambda I)\).

notation.meaning: eigenspace associated with the repeated eigenvalue

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Eigenvector nonuniqueness for repeated eigenvalues is standard, but the asserted branching instability and prescribed basis-invariant width criterion require a branching-specific source.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Based Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses violation of the lifted rank-one relation to choose a branching projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a node, solve a lifted relaxation with variables \((x,X)\) and require \(R=X-xx^T\succeq0\). If \(R=0\), the rank-one relation is satisfied. Otherwise compute a unit eigenvector \(v\) for \(\lambda_{\max}(R)>0\), determine \(a=\min_{z\in P}v^Tz\) and \(b=\max_{z\in P}v^Tz\), choose \(t\in(a,b)\), and create children imposing \(v^Tx\le t\) and \(v^Tx\ge t\), respectively. The selected direction maximizes \(v^TRv\) over unit vectors and therefore targets the largest spectral violation of \(X=xx^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch along the leading eigenvector of the lifted rank residual, targeting the direction with the largest violation of the rank-one relation.
assumptions_latex: The node domain \(P\) is nonempty and compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A leading eigenvector \(v\) maximizes \(u^TRu\) over \(\|u\|_2=1\) and defines the branching projection.

notation.meaning: lifted surrogate for the matrix xx transpose

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The leading residual eigenvector identifies the largest Rayleigh-quotient violation, but no source supports the complete branching rule or threshold policy as a rank-based QCQP method.

children.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
children.top_down_role: Selection and interpretation of lower bounds within spatial search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Relaxation Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes valid lower bounds supplied by a lifted node relaxation in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the feasible set of a minimization QCQP on node domain \(P\), and let \(R_P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) be a lifted relaxation such that, for every \(x\in F_P\), there exists \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \((x,z)\in R_P\) and \(\underline f(x,z)\le f(x)\). Then \(L(P)=\inf_{(x,z)\in R_P}\underline f(x,z)\) satisfies \(L(P)\le\inf_{x\in F_P}f(x)\). More generally, any certified value \(D(P)\le L(P)\), including a valid dual bound, is a node lower bound. If \(R_P=\varnothing\), then \(F_P=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lifted relaxation representing every node-feasible point with an underestimating objective yields a valid node lower bound. A certified dual bound below the relaxation optimum is also valid, and relaxation infeasibility proves node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: For every \(x\in F_P\), some \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \((x,z)\in R_P\) and \(\underline f(x,z)\le f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(P)\le\inf_{x\in F_P}f(x)\); every certified \(D(P)\le L(P)\) is also a valid node lower bound, and \(R_P=\varnothing\) implies \(F_P=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: original feasible set at node P
lifted relaxed feasible set at node P
optimal value of the node relaxation
certified lower bound on the relaxation optimal value

children.title: Fathoming Criteria
children.top_down_role: Node elimination regimes based on feasibility, bounds, dominance, or tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Fathoming Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives safe pruning tests for a minimization spatial branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a node \(P\), let \(L(P)\) be a valid lower bound, let \(U\) be the objective value of a feasible incumbent, and fix \(\varepsilon\ge0\). The node may be fathomed if at least one condition holds: its relaxation is infeasible; \(L(P)\ge U-\varepsilon\); or a certified terminal procedure has solved the node to tolerance and produced no point improving \(U-\varepsilon\). The first test excludes node feasibility, while the latter two certify that the node cannot contain a solution whose objective improves the incumbent by more than \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a node when it is infeasible, its lower bound cannot improve the incumbent beyond tolerance, or it has been solved to the required tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any listed condition safely permits removal of \(P\) from the active-node set for \(\varepsilon\)-global optimization.

notation.meaning: valid lower bound for node P

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides a spectral difference-of-convex representation of an indefinite quadratic function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^TQx+c^Tx+d\) with \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\). Write the spectral decomposition \(Q=Q_+-Q_-\), where \(Q_+\succeq0\) and \(Q_-\succeq0\) are formed from the positive and negative eigenvalue parts of \(Q\). Then \(q=g-h\), where \(g(x)=x^TQ_+x+c^Tx+d\) and \(h(x)=x^TQ_-x\). Both \(g\) and \(h\) are convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). The decomposition is not unique: any common positive-semidefinite quadratic term may be added to both components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every symmetric quadratic is the difference of two convex quadratics obtained by separating its positive and negative spectral parts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=g(x)-h(x)\) with convex quadratic functions \(g\) and \(h\).

notation.meaning: absolute negative spectral part of Q

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Shift Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexifies an indefinite quadratic by shifting its Hessian and isolating a concave norm term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^TQx+c^Tx+d\) with \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n\). For any \(\alpha\ge\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\), define \(g_\alpha(x)=x^T(Q+\alpha I)x+c^Tx+d\). Then \(Q+\alpha I\succeq0\), so \(g_\alpha\) is convex, and \(q(x)=g_\alpha(x)-\alpha\|x\|_2^2\). The smallest scalar shift producing positive semidefiniteness is \(\alpha^*=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(Q)\}\); larger shifts remain valid but introduce a stronger concave component that must subsequently be relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a sufficient identity shift makes the quadratic part convex, while subtracting the same multiple of the squared norm preserves the original function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(x)=g_\alpha(x)-\alpha\|x\|_2^2\) and \(g_\alpha\) is convex.

knowledge_statements.title: AlphaBB Quadratic Underestimators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the box-valid alphaBB convex underestimator and its curvature condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be twice continuously differentiable on the box \(B=[l,u]\subset\mathbb{R}^n\). For \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}_+^n\), define \(f_\alpha(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i(l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\). Since \((l_i-x_i)(u_i-x_i)\le0\) on \(B\), one has \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\). Moreover, \(f_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\) whenever \(\nabla^2f(x)+2\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in B\). For a quadratic with Hessian \(2Q\), this condition reduces to \(Q+\operatorname{Diag}(\alpha)\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AlphaBB adds nonpositive separable box terms to obtain a convex global underestimator when the diagonal shifts make every Hessian positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_\alpha\) is convex on \(B\) and satisfies \(f_\alpha(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise Convex Envelopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines exact cellwise convex envelopes into a partition-based lower bound and records refinement monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the union of finitely many compact convex cells \(P_j\), and let \(f_j^{\mathrm{cv}}\) be the exact convex envelope of a real-valued function \(f\) on \(P_j\). Then \(f_j^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in P_j\), so \(L=\min_j\inf_{x\in P_j}f_j^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)\) satisfies \(L\le\inf_{x\in P}f(x)\). If each parent cell is partitioned into compact convex subcells and exact envelopes are recomputed, the refined lower bound is at least \(L\), because the restriction of a parent-cell envelope to any subcell is a convex underestimator there and is therefore dominated by the subcell's exact convex envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact convex envelopes on compact convex cells provide a valid global lower bound. Recomputing exact envelopes on a convex refinement cannot weaken that bound.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the union of finitely many compact convex cells \(P_j\).
Each \(f_j^{\mathrm{cv}}\) is the exact convex envelope of the real-valued function \(f\) on \(P_j\).
Every refined cell is a compact convex subset of its parent cell.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\min_j\inf_{x\in P_j}f_j^{\mathrm{cv}}(x)\le\inf_{x\in P}f(x)\), and the corresponding exact-envelope lower bound is nondecreasing under refinement.

notation.meaning: exact convex envelope of f on cell j

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Based Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteratively contracts variable bounds using necessary consequences of quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a box \(B=[l,u]\) and quadratic constraints \(q_r(x)\le0\), initialize \(B^{(0)}=B\). For each constraint and variable, use interval bounds for all terms not being isolated to derive a necessary univariate quadratic inequality for \(x_i\); intersect its solution set with the current interval of \(x_i\), retaining an interval hull when necessary. Sweep through all constraint-variable pairs until no bound changes beyond tolerance or an interval becomes empty. The output box \(B'\) satisfies \(\{x\in B:q_r(x)\le0\ \forall r\}\subseteq B'\subseteq B\); an empty output certifies infeasibility of the original box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagate quadratic constraints through variable intervals until stable; the contracted box retains every feasible point, and an empty interval proves node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: All initial variable bounds are finite.
Every interval evaluation used in propagation is inclusion-valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned box \(B'\) contains every feasible point in \(B\); \(B'=\varnothing\) certifies infeasibility.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inclusion guarantee depends on the precise interval isolation and hull operations. A source is required for this algorithmic variant and its feasibility-preservation claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound tightening over a valid QCQP relaxation at a branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the node relaxation have feasible set \(R\subseteq[\ell,u]\) and contain the original node-feasible set \(F\). For every selected coordinate \(j\), solve \(L_j=\inf\{x_j:x\in R\}\) and \(U_j=\sup\{x_j:x\in R\}\). If both problems have certified finite optima, update \(\ell_j\leftarrow\max\{\ell_j,L_j\}\) and \(u_j\leftarrow\min\{u_j,U_j\}\). If either subproblem is solved only to a valid bound, use that bound in the corresponding direction. Repeat until no bound improves beyond a prescribed tolerance. If \(R=\varnothing\), declare the node infeasible; otherwise return the tightened box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize each variable over a valid relaxation and intersect the resulting extrema with its current interval; relaxation infeasibility safely eliminates the node.
assumptions_latex: All reported optimization bounds are globally valid for their relaxation subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq[\ell',u']\subseteq[\ell,u]\), and \(R=\varnothing\Rightarrow F=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Constraint Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval propagation by isolating one variable in a quadratic inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a valid constraint \(a x_j^2+b x_j+r(x_{-j})\leq0\) on the current box \(B=[\ell,u]\). Compute a certified lower bound \(\rho\leq r(x_{-j})\) for every \(x\in B\). Form \(S_j=[\ell_j,u_j]\cap\{t\in\mathbb R:a t^2+b t+\rho\leq0\}\) and replace the interval of \(x_j\) by the interval hull \(\operatorname{hull}(S_j)\). If \(S_j=\varnothing\), declare the box infeasible. Apply this operation across constraints and variables until a complete pass produces no material contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound the remaining terms, solve the resulting univariate quadratic inequality, and intersect its solution with the selected variable’s interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\cap B\subseteq\{x\in B:x_j\in\operatorname{hull}(S_j)\}\), and \(S_j=\varnothing\Rightarrow F\cap B=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Separation for Lifted QCQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of violated valid inequalities in a lifted QCQP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=(x,X)\) denote lifted variables, with \(X\) representing \(xx^{\mathsf T}\), and let \(C\) be a chosen family of valid inequalities \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}y\leq\beta\) for the lifted feasible set. At a relaxation solution \(\bar y\), solve the normalized separation problem \(v^*=\sup\{\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar y-\beta:(\alpha,\beta)\in C,\ \|\alpha\|_*\leq1\}\). If \(v^*>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\), add the maximizing inequality and reoptimize the relaxation; otherwise declare that no inequality in the normalized family is violated beyond tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize normalized violation over a valid lifted-cut family, add a positively violated cut, and reoptimize until no such cut remains.
assumptions_latex: Every \((\alpha,\beta)\in C\) defines an inequality valid for all lifted feasible points.
The separation optimum or a certified violated member of \(C\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\Rightarrow\alpha^{*\mathsf T}\bar y>\beta^*\) while \(\alpha^{*\mathsf T}y\leq\beta^*\) for every lifted feasible \(y\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multistart Local Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite multistart generation of feasible QCQP incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact search box \(B\), choose starts \(s^1,\ldots,s^N\in B\) by a prescribed grid, randomized distribution, or space-filling design. From each \(s^k\), run a terminating constrained local solver, possibly after feasibility restoration, and retain every returned feasible point \(x^k\). For a minimization QCQP, output \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x^k):x^k\text{ is feasible}\}\). If no run returns a feasible point, report failure to generate an incumbent, not infeasibility of the QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a local constrained solver from multiple starts and retain the best feasible result; failure of all runs does not prove infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N\) is finite and each local-solver call terminates.
Candidate feasibility is checked against the QCQP constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve a valid relaxation and obtain a solution \(\bar y\), whose original-variable component is \(\bar x\), together with any relaxation-derived activity or branching scores. Construct finitely many starts by projecting \(\bar x\) and selected perturbations onto the variable domain. Order starts using the relaxation scores, run a constrained local QCQP solver from each, and verify every returned point in the original constraints. For minimization, return the verified feasible point of smallest objective value, or report that the search found no incumbent. Neither relaxation feasibility nor search failure is treated as primal feasibility or infeasibility.

children.title: Relaxation Rounding
children.top_down_role: Candidate generation from continuous or lifted relaxation solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized rounding from a positive-semidefinite lifted relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a lifted relaxation point \((\bar x,\bar X)\) satisfying \(\Sigma=\bar X-\bar x\bar x^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), choose a factor \(L\) with \(LL^{\mathsf T}=\Sigma\). For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), draw \(\xi^k\) with mean zero and identity covariance, form \(z^k=\bar x+L\xi^k\), and project \(z^k\) onto the variable box and any explicitly roundable discrete domains. Pass the resulting candidates to feasibility repair and original-constraint checking. Output the best verified feasible candidate, if one exists; otherwise report rounding failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample candidates using the lifted relaxation’s mean and covariance, project domain-restricted variables, and accept only candidates surviving repair and feasibility checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[z^k]=\bar x\) and \(\operatorname{Cov}(z^k)=\bar X-\bar x\bar x^{\mathsf T}\) before projection.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports this lifted randomized-rounding formulation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moment calculation before projection is mathematically consistent, but no source is supplied for interpreting the lifted slack matrix as a sampling covariance and using the resulting randomized procedure as QCQP relaxation rounding. Source uncertainty therefore affects the intended algorithmic formulation.

children.title: Feasibility Repair
children.top_down_role: Restoration of constraint satisfaction for rounded candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalty-based restoration of a rounded QCQP candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \(z\in D\), inequality constraints \(g_i(x)\leq0\), and equality constraints \(h_j(x)=0\), define \(V(x)=\sum_i[\max\{g_i(x),0\}]^2+\sum_j h_j(x)^2\). Starting at \(z\), approximately minimize \(\tfrac12\|x-z\|_2^2+\rho V(x)\) over the variable domain \(D\), increasing \(\rho>0\) when violation stagnates. Stop with a repaired point only when independently evaluated residuals satisfy \(g_i(x)\leq\tau\) and \(|h_j(x)|\leq\tau\); otherwise return repair failure after the prescribed iteration or penalty limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize distance to the rounded candidate plus constraint violation, increasing the penalty as needed, and accept only a separately checked tolerance-feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i g_i(x)\leq\tau\) and \(\max_j|h_j(x)|\leq\tau\) whenever repair succeeds.

children.title: Repair Failure Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Repair Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local repair can fail when its neighborhood misses a disconnected feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the one-variable QCQP with domain \([-1,1]\) and equality \(x^2=1\), whose feasible set is \(F=\{-1,1\}\). Let rounding return \(z=0\), and let repair be restricted to the trust region \(|x-z|\leq\delta\) with \(0\leq\delta<1\). Then the repair subproblem contains no feasible point although the original QCQP is feasible. Consequently, failure of a neighborhood-restricted repair procedure cannot certify global infeasibility; expansion, restart, or a global feasibility method is required to reach either component of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local repair neighborhood may miss every component of a disconnected feasible set, so repair failure is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The repair iterates are constrained by \(|x-z|\leq\delta\) with \(z=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) but \(F\cap\{x:|x-z|\leq\delta\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). Suppose \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\in F\) is verified feasible with \(U=f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\), and a valid relaxation supplies a certified lower bound \(L\leq f^*\). Then \(0\leq U-f^*\leq U-L\). Hence \((x^{\mathrm{inc}},L)\) is an absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global-optimality certificate whenever \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\). If \(U=L\), the incumbent is globally optimal. Both feasibility of the incumbent and validity of the relaxation bound are necessary parts of the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible incumbent gives an upper bound and a valid relaxation gives a lower bound; their difference bounds the incumbent's global suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global certificate obtained by exhausting a finite branch-and-bound partition.

source_refs.locator: 2.7.2 A Branch-and-Bound Algorithm Scheme for Lipschitzian Optimization p. 132
7.3 Cut and Split (Branch and Bound) Methods p. 176

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set, let \(f^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\cap D\}\), and let \(D_1,\ldots,D_N\) cover the original domain \(D\). Let \(L_k\) be a certified lower bound on \(f\) over \(F\cap D_k\). Given a verified feasible incumbent of value \(U\), mark region \(D_k\) exhausted if \(F\cap D_k=\varnothing\) is certified or \(L_k\geq U-\varepsilon\). If every region is exhausted and the cover has no omitted region, then every feasible \(x\in D\) satisfies \(f(x)\geq U-\varepsilon\). Thus the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-globally optimal; for \(\varepsilon=0\), it is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a finite domain cover is complete and every region is infeasible or bounded no better than the incumbent, the incumbent is globally certified.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conic dual-ray certificate proving infeasibility of a QCQP relaxation and hence the QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a valid conic relaxation be \(R=\{z\in K:Az=b\}\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone, and suppose the original lifted feasible set is contained in \(R\). A vector \(y\) satisfying \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) is an infeasibility certificate: any \(z\in R\) would give \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\langle A^{\mathsf T}y,z\rangle\geq0\), a contradiction. Therefore \(R=\varnothing\), and containment implies that the original QCQP is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic dual ray contradicts every relaxation-feasible point; because the relaxation contains the QCQP feasible set, it also proves QCQP infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a closed convex cone with dual \(K^*\).
The original lifted feasible set is contained in \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R=\varnothing\), hence \(F=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Certificate Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed-rounding validation of computed QCQP bounds and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Recompute every claimed certificate quantity using interval arithmetic with outward rounding. For a proposed incumbent \(\hat x\), require interval evaluations \(G_i(\hat x)\) to satisfy \(\sup G_i(\hat x)\leq\tau_p\), and equality intervals \(H_j(\hat x)\) to satisfy \(\sup\{|t|:t\in H_j(\hat x)\}\leq\tau_p\). Validate relaxation dual feasibility with residual tolerance \(\tau_d\), and derive a downward-rounded lower bound \(\underline L\); derive an upward-rounded incumbent value \(\overline U\). Accept an absolute gap certificate only if \(\overline U-\underline L\leq\varepsilon\), recording all tolerances and intervals used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute feasibility, dual validity, and objective bounds with outward-rounded intervals, accepting a gap only when the worst-case enclosed gap meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Interval evaluations enclose the exact real-arithmetic quantities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f^*\in[\underline L,\overline U]\) and \(\overline U-\underline L\leq\varepsilon\) for an accepted validated certificate.

notation.meaning: Recorded primal and dual residual tolerances

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Polynomial-Time Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak polynomial-time solvability of rational convex QCQPs to prescribed additive accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider 
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} x^{\mathsf T}Q_0x+2q_0^{\mathsf T}x+r_0\quad\text{subject to}\quad x^{\mathsf T}Q_ix+2q_i^{\mathsf T}x+r_i\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m.\]
If every \(Q_i\succeq0\), including \(Q_0\), the feasible set and objective are convex. Given rational data, a rational radius bound containing an optimizer, and \(\varepsilon>0\), standard convex-optimization methods compute a feasible \(x_\varepsilon\) whose value is at most \(\varepsilon\) above the optimum in time polynomial in the input bit length, \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\), and the radius-bound encoding length, under a polynomially usable separation-oracle or interior-point regularity model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational convex QCQP is solvable to additive accuracy in polynomial time when boundedness and the required oracle or regularity data are available.
assumptions_latex: The rational instance includes an encoded optimizer-radius bound.
The computational model supplies polynomial-time separation or suitable interior-point regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible point is computable in time polynomial in the encoded input and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).

notation.meaning: The symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Constraint Hidden-Convexity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real trust-region-type QCQP under the strict-feasibility form of the S-lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Ax+2a^{\mathsf T}x+\alpha\) and \(g(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Bx+2b^{\mathsf T}x+\beta\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with symmetric \(A,B\). If some \(\bar x\) satisfies \(g(\bar x)<0\) and the primal infimum \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le0\}\) is finite, then
\[p^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda g(x)\bigr).\]
Equivalently, for every \(t<p^*\), there exists \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(f(x)-t+\lambda g(x)\ge0\) for all \(x\). Thus one quadratic constraint admits an exact semidefinite certificate despite possible nonconvexity of the original formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict feasibility makes the one-constraint quadratic problem satisfy exact Lagrangian duality and an S-lemma semidefinite certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A,B\in\mathbb S^n\) and all remaining coefficients are real.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^*=\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\inf_x(f(x)+\lambda g(x))\), with the equivalent global nonnegativity certificate.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the single-constraint QCQP.
Nonnegative multiplier for the quadratic constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strict-feasibility S-lemma formulation, finite-value hypothesis, and duality content fit this hidden-convexity leaf, and duality is the correct content kind. No citation is supplied, so the exact hypotheses and dual conclusion require an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Fixed-Dimension Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior when ambient or effective dimension is fixed.

assumptions_latex: The dimension \(n\) is a fixed constant.
For optimization, \(S\) is compact and an accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is polynomial in the remaining encoded input for each fixed \(n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity regime for rational quadratic feasibility with fixed ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(n\). Given rational quadratic polynomials \(q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb Q[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), deciding whether
\[S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:q_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\]
is empty, and optimizing a rational quadratic objective over a compact such \(S\) to additive accuracy \(\varepsilon\), can be performed by real-algebraic decision methods with running time polynomial in the coefficient bit length, \(m\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\); the polynomial degree and constants may depend on fixed \(n\). The statement does not assert uniform polynomial time when \(n\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic feasibility and bounded optimization are polynomial-time for every fixed dimension, although the polynomial may deteriorate with dimension.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Dimension Regimes

children.title: Fixed-Structure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity behavior under fixed rank, sparsity, constraint count, or graph structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Structure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal fixed-parameter criterion for a structural QCQP tractability regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\kappa(I)\) be a structural parameter of a rational QCQP instance \(I\), such as interaction-graph treewidth, aggregate quadratic rank, or the number of nonconvex directions. A fixed-structure regime is fixed-parameter tractable only if there exist a computable function \(F\), a constant \(c\) independent of \(\kappa\), and an algorithm returning the required exact or \(\varepsilon\)-accurate solution with running time
\[T(I,\varepsilon)\le F(\kappa(I))\bigl(|I|+\log(1/\varepsilon)\bigr)^c.\]
Merely proving polynomial time separately for each fixed parameter value, with exponent depending on that value, establishes an XP regime rather than fixed-parameter tractability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structural restriction is fixed-parameter tractable only when its parameter affects the multiplicative factor, not the polynomial exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finitely encoded rational QCQP instance.
\(\kappa(I)\in\mathbb N\) is the declared structural parameter.
The approximation convention, if used, is additive \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: FPT requires \(T\le F(\kappa)(|I|+\log(1/\varepsilon))^c\) with \(c\) parameter-independent.

notation.meaning: Chosen structural parameter of the instance.
Binary encoding length of the instance.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly distinguishes an FPT running-time form from XP, and condition is an appropriate role for this structural-regime leaf. The illustrative QCQP parameters are not asserted to be tractable, but the parameterized-complexity definitions still require a specific authoritative citation.

children.title: Parameter-Dependence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transitions caused by allowing previously fixed dimensions or structural parameters to grow.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Dependence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating FPT, XP, and unrestricted polynomial-time claims for parameterized QCQPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a parameterized QCQP family \((I,k)), the bound \(T(I,k)=f(k)|I|^c\) with constant \(c\) is fixed-parameter tractable, whereas \(T(I,k)=|I|^{g(k)}\) establishes only membership in XP. If the parameter is allowed to grow with the input, neither bound yields ordinary polynomial time unless \(f(k)\) and the exponent remain polynomially controlled in \(|I|\). Consequently, a tractability statement obtained by fixing dimension, rank, constraint count, or sparsity width cannot be extrapolated to unrestricted QCQP without an explicit uniform dependence bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polynomial time for every fixed parameter is not necessarily uniform polynomial time; parameter-dependent exponents mark the XP boundary.
assumptions_latex: \(|I|\) denotes binary input length and \(k\in\mathbb N\) the parameter.
The exponent \(c\) in an FPT bound is independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bound \(f(k)|I|^c\) is FPT, while \(|I|^{g(k)}\) is generally only XP and does not imply unrestricted polynomial time.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The FPT-versus-XP boundary matches the leaf and failure_boundary is the correct content kind. A source is needed for the formal classification, and the phrase 'polynomially controlled' must be checked against a precise uniform-complexity formulation before the unrestricted-polynomial-time conclusion can be accepted.

assumptions_latex: The source binary quadratic optimization instance has finitely encoded rational data.
Quadratic equalities may be represented by pairs of quadratic inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact global optimization of unrestricted rational QCQPs is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case hardness of unrestricted rational QCQP through an exact binary encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Unrestricted rational QCQP is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions. In particular, binary quadratic optimization with rational data reduces to QCQP by imposing \(x_i(x_i-1)=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with each equality representable by two quadratic inequalities. The reduction preserves feasible points and objective values and has polynomial encoding size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact global optimization of unrestricted rational QCQPs is NP-hard through a polynomial-size quadratic encoding of binary variables.

assumptions_latex: The weighted graph has nonnegative rational weights and at least one edge.
Quadratic equalities are permitted as QCQP constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hardness persists when nonconvexity is concentrated in an indefinite quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Global minimization of a rational QCQP is NP-hard even when its objective matrix is indefinite. A polynomial reduction from weighted MAX-CUT may use the sign constraints \(x_i^2=1\), an auxiliary variable \(y=0\), and the objective matrix \(Q=\operatorname{diag}(-L,1)\), where \(L\) is the graph Laplacian. For every input graph having at least one edge, \(Q\) has both a negative and a positive eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MAX-CUT reduces polynomially to a QCQP with a genuinely indefinite objective matrix, so global minimization in this regime is NP-hard.

assumptions_latex: The source binary linear feasibility instance has rational encoded data.
Bounds \(0\le x_i\le1\) are included for every variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: QCQP feasibility with separable nonconvex quadratic constraints is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Separable concave quadratic constraint enforcing binarity on the unit interval.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary feasibility encoded by separable concave quadratic inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: QCQP feasibility is NP-hard even with a constant objective, linear side constraints, and separable nonconvex quadratic constraints. For variables satisfying \(0\le x_i\le1\), the constraints \(x_i(1-x_i)\le0\) enforce \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), giving a polynomial reduction from binary linear feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separable concave quadratic constraints can enforce binary variables, making QCQP feasibility NP-hard even with a constant objective.

assumptions_latex: Binary quadratic optimization is the source problem.
The number of quadratic inequalities may grow linearly with \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact QCQP optimization with an unbounded number of quadratic constraints is NP-hard.

notation.meaning: Number of quadratic inequalities used to encode the binary equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the one-constraint hidden-convexity phenomenon under many quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact QCQP optimization is NP-hard when the number of quadratic constraints may grow with the input. Binary restrictions can be encoded using the \(2n\) inequalities \(x_i(x_i-1)\le0\) and \(-x_i(x_i-1)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), preserving the feasible points and objective values of a binary quadratic optimization instance. Hence the one-constraint S-lemma regime does not extend to an unbounded collection of quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An input-sized family of simple quadratic constraints can encode binary optimization, so one-constraint exactness does not imply tractability for many constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Constraint Hardness

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) if and only if \(x_i^2-x_i=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact quadratic representation of binary decisions by polynomial equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), the system \(x_i^2-x_i=0\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,n\) is equivalent to \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). These \(n\) quadratic equations give a polynomial-size exact representation of binary decisions inside a QCQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equations x_i squared minus x_i equals zero give an exact polynomial-size representation of binary decisions in a QCQP.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Encoding Hardness
Semidefinite-Rounding Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random-hyperplane rounding of the canonical semidefinite relaxation for weighted MAX-CUT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given nonnegative weights \(w_{ij}\), solve
\[\max \frac12\sum_{i<j}w_{ij}(1-X_{ij})\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\succeq0,\quad X_{ii}=1.\]
Factor an optimal solution as \(X=V^{\mathsf T}V\) with unit columns \(v_i\). Draw \(g\sim N(0,I)\), set \(s_i=1\) when \(g^{\mathsf T}v_i\ge0\) and \(s_i=-1\) otherwise, and output the cut determined by \(s\). Independent repetitions may return the best sampled cut. Its expected weight is at least \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\) times the optimum, where
\[\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}=\min_{0\le\theta\le\pi}\frac{2\theta}{\pi(1-\cos\theta)}\approx0.87856.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the MAX-CUT SDP and randomly separate its unit vectors by a hyperplane, obtaining the Goemans–Williamson expected approximation ratio.
assumptions_latex: The semidefinite relaxation is solved to sufficient numerical accuracy.
The rounding vector is standard Gaussian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected cut value is at least \(\alpha_{\mathrm{GW}}\) times the optimal cut value.

notation.meaning: Positive-semidefinite Gram matrix of relaxation vectors.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The SDP, Gaussian hyperplane rounding procedure, and approximation constant are internally consistent, and algorithm is the correct role for this approximation-family leaf. The primary Goemans-Williamson source or another authoritative theorem-level locator is required to support the expected approximation ratio.

knowledge_statements.title: Real-Field Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real Gaussian sign-rounding guarantee for positive-semidefinite binary quadratic maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and define
\[\operatorname{OPT}=\max_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}x^{\mathsf T}Qx,\qquad \operatorname{SDP}=\max\{\langle Q,X\rangle:X\succeq0,\ X_{ii}=1\}.\]
For an optimal real Gram representation \(X_{ij}=v_i^{\mathsf T}v_j\), draw \(g\sim N(0,I)\) and set \(x_i=\operatorname{sign}(g^{\mathsf T}v_i)\). Then
\[\mathbb E[x^{\mathsf T}Qx]\ge\frac{2}{\pi}\operatorname{SDP}\ge\frac{2}{\pi}\operatorname{OPT}.\]
Thus real-field semidefinite rounding supplies a polynomial-time randomized \(2/\pi\)-approximation for this positive-semidefinite quadratic family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real Gaussian sign rounding gives a randomized 2/π approximation for positive-semidefinite binary quadratic maximization.
assumptions_latex: The SDP is solved to sufficient accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[x^{\mathsf T}Qx]\ge(2/\pi)\operatorname{OPT}\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the real semidefinite relaxation.

children.title: Complex-Field Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation behavior for QCQP formulated over complex variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Complex-Field Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies approximation guarantees for homogeneous complex QCQPs under multiplicative maximization ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A complex-field approximation regime is a class of problems 
\[\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathbb C}=\max\{z^*Q_0z:z\in\mathbb C^n,\ z^*Q_i z\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\]
where every \(Q_i\) is Hermitian and the objective is nonnegative on the feasible set, together with a polynomial-time algorithm producing a feasible \(\widehat z\) such that \(\widehat z^*Q_0\widehat z\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathbb C}\). The factor \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) may depend on specified parameters such as \(m\), but not on numerical encoding length unless stated explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complex-field regime specifies a complex Hermitian QCQP class and a polynomial-time feasible solution attaining a stated fraction of its nonnegative optimum.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty and \(z^*Q_0z\ge0\) on it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat z^*Q_0\widehat z\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}_{\mathbb C}\).

notation.meaning: conjugate transpose of the complex vector z

review_flags: Exact field-specific approximation factors depend on the constraint family and require a specialized QCQP source.

children.title: Field-Dependent Approximation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Differences in attainable guarantees and relaxation gaps across scalar fields.

knowledge_statements.title: Field-Dependent Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares best achievable ratios after fixing matched real and complex QCQP families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For matched maximization families \(\mathcal P_{\mathbb R}\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathbb C}\), let \(\rho_{\mathbb F}(I)\in[0,1]\) be the guaranteed value-to-optimum ratio of a specified approximation method on instance \(I\) over \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\). The instancewise field gap is
\[\Delta(I)=\rho_{\mathbb C}(I)-\rho_{\mathbb R}(I).\]
For parameter class \(\mathcal I_k\), the worst-case field gap is \(\Delta_k=\inf_{I\in\mathcal I_k}\rho_{\mathbb C}(I)-\inf_{I\in\mathcal I_k}\rho_{\mathbb R}(I)\). A nonzero value records a field-dependent approximation regime, provided the formulations and computational models are matched.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The field gap is the difference between approximation guarantees for matched complex and real QCQP families under the same method and computational model.
assumptions_latex: Real and complex instances are matched by identical coefficient data and constraint templates.
Both ratios use the same objective orientation and approximation convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_k\ne0\) identifies a field-dependent worst-case guarantee.

notation.meaning: worst-case field-dependent gap for parameter class k

review_flags: A specialized source is needed to attach sharp real-versus-complex constants to this comparison.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison is coherent, but a source is needed to establish the intended matching between real and complex instance families and the relevant approximation guarantees.

children.title: Homogeneous Approximation Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers QCQPs whose objective and constraints are quadratic forms without affine terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A homogeneous QCQP approximation regime consists of instances
\[\max\{x^*Q_0x:x\in\mathbb F^n,\ x^*Q_i x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\]
with \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\), symmetric or Hermitian matrices \(Q_i\), and no linear or constant terms in the quadratic expressions. An \(\alpha\)-approximation algorithm for a nonnegative maximization regime returns a feasible \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(\widehat x^*Q_0\widehat x\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\), where the permitted dependence of \(\alpha\) on \(m\), rank, or other structural parameters is part of the regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous regime treats quadratic-form objectives and constraints and specifies the structural parameters controlling a multiplicative approximation factor.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\) is symmetric over \(\mathbb R\) or Hermitian over \(\mathbb C\).
The optimum is finite and nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x^*Q_0\widehat x\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\).

children.title: Inhomogeneous Approximation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Approximation behavior in the presence of affine or constant terms.

knowledge_statements.title: Inhomogeneous Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers QCQPs containing linear or constant terms, their approximation guarantees, and their explicitly normalized homogeneous lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\). An inhomogeneous QCQP approximation regime consists of problems
\[\max\{f_0(x):x\in\mathbb F^n,\ f_i(x)\le 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\},\]
where \(f_i(x)=x^*Q_i x+2\operatorname{Re}(q_i^*x)+c_i\), each \(Q_i\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}\) is symmetric or Hermitian, each \(q_i\in\mathbb F^n\), each \(c_i\in\mathbb R\), and at least one \(q_i\) or \(c_i\) is nonzero. For a nonnegative maximization regime with finite optimum \(\operatorname{OPT}\), an \(\alpha\)-approximation returns a feasible \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(f_0(\widehat x)\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\). Introducing \(y=(x,t)\) and
\[\widetilde Q_i=\begin{pmatrix}Q_i&q_i\\q_i^*&c_i\end{pmatrix}\]
gives \(f_i(x)=y^*\widetilde Q_i y\) when \(t=1\). Thus equivalence with the original QCQP requires \(t=1\), or a phase-equivalent normalization justified by the formulation; dropping that normalization defines a different relaxation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inhomogeneous approximation regime specifies a QCQP with affine or constant terms, its approximation convention, and a homogeneous lift that remains equivalent only under an appropriate normalization of the added coordinate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}\), with symmetric matrices over \(\mathbb R\) and Hermitian matrices over \(\mathbb C\).
\(Q_i\in\mathbb F^{n\times n}\), \(q_i\in\mathbb F^n\), and \(c_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=0,\ldots,m\).
At least one \(q_i\) or \(c_i\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y^*\widetilde Q_i y=f_i(x)\) when \(y=(x,1)\), and an \(\alpha\)-approximation satisfies \(f_0(\widehat x)\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\).

children.title: Homogenization Gap Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Homogenization Gap Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when lifting preserves an inhomogeneous QCQP and when a relaxed normalizing coordinate can create a gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the feasible set of an inhomogeneous QCQP and let \(H_1\) be its lifted feasible set with \(y=(x,t)\) and \(t=1\). The map \(x\mapsto(x,1)\) preserves every objective and constraint value, so \(\operatorname{OPT}(H_1)=\operatorname{OPT}(F)\). If normalization is weakened to a set \(T\) containing values other than \(1\), the enlarged lifted set \(H_T\) satisfies \(H_1\subseteq H_T\); for maximization, \(\operatorname{OPT}(H_T)\ge\operatorname{OPT}(F)\). Strict inequality is possible and marks the homogenization-gap boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homogenization is exact with a fixed added coordinate. Relaxing that normalization enlarges the feasible set and can strictly improve a maximization bound.
assumptions_latex: The lifted matrices encode the original affine quadratics exactly at \(t=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}(H_1)=\operatorname{OPT}(F)\), while \(H_1\subseteq H_T\) implies \(\operatorname{OPT}(H_T)\ge\operatorname{OPT}(F)\).

notation.meaning: lifted feasible set with t fixed to one
lifted feasible set with t allowed in T

review_flags: A source with an explicit QCQP homogenization-gap example is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exactness under fixed normalization and monotonicity under feasible-set enlargement are correct, but the asserted possibility of strict inequality requires an explicit sourced QCQP example.

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Restricted Approximation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies QCQP approximation guarantees conditional on coefficient, variable, or quadratic-form sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sign-restricted approximation regime is a QCQP family in which a declared sign predicate \(S\) is imposed on the data or variables, such as \(x\ge0\), entrywise \(Q_i\ge0\), or \(x^*Q_0x\ge0\) throughout the feasible set. For a maximization family with finite \(\operatorname{OPT}\ge0\), its approximation factor is the largest stated \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) for which a polynomial-time method always returns feasible \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(f_0(\widehat x)\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\). The predicate \(S\) is part of the theorem hypotheses and cannot be discarded when transferring the guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign-restricted regime states the precise sign condition under which a polynomial-time QCQP approximation ratio is guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: The sign predicate \(S\) is explicitly specified.
The maximization objective and optimum are nonnegative and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_0(\widehat x)\ge\alpha\operatorname{OPT}\) for every instance satisfying \(S\).

notation.meaning: declared sign predicate on variables, matrices, or quadratic values

review_flags: The node does not identify which sign predicate or sharp approximation theorem is intended.

children.title: Approximation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Loss between an approximation output and the underlying QCQP optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines multiplicative and additive loss of a feasible approximate QCQP solution relative to the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a maximization QCQP with finite optimum \(v^*>0\) and feasible approximate solution \(\widehat x\), the multiplicative approximation gap is
\[g_{\mathrm{app}}^{\times}=1-\frac{f(\widehat x)}{v^*},\]
and the additive approximation gap is \(g_{\mathrm{app}}^{+}=v^*-f(\widehat x)\). If \(0\le f(\widehat x)\le v^*\), then both gaps are nonnegative and \(g_{\mathrm{app}}^{+}=v^*g_{\mathrm{app}}^{\times}\). An \(\alpha\)-approximation is equivalently characterized by \(g_{\mathrm{app}}^{\times}\le1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The approximation gap measures objective loss of a feasible computed point, either absolutely or as a fraction of the positive optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{\mathrm{app}}^{+}=v^*g_{\mathrm{app}}^{\times}\) and \(f(\widehat x)\ge\alpha v^*\iff g_{\mathrm{app}}^{\times}\le1-\alpha\).

children.title: Relaxation Gaps
children.top_down_role: Separation between a relaxation value and the underlying QCQP optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the discrepancy between a QCQP optimum and an outer-relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq R\) be respectively the feasible sets of a maximization QCQP and its outer relaxation, and define \(v^*=\sup_{x\in F}f(x)\) and \(u^*=\sup_{y\in R}\widetilde f(y)\), with \(\widetilde f=f\) on embedded points of \(F\). The additive relaxation gap is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{+}=u^*-v^*\ge0\). When \(0<v^*\le u^*<\infty\), the multiplicative relaxation factor is \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\times}=u^*/v^*\ge1\). Exactness means \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{+}=0\), equivalently \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{\times}=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation gap compares the original maximization optimum with the upper bound obtained from a containing relaxed feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The relaxed objective agrees with the original objective on embedded feasible points.
The compared optimal values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^*\ge v^*\), hence \(g_{\mathrm{rel}}^{+}\ge0\).

children.title: Gap Transfer Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where relaxation quality controls or fails to control approximation quality.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Transfer Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers a rounding guarantee relative to an outer-relaxation value into a guarantee relative to the QCQP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a nonnegative maximization QCQP with optimum \(v^*\) and an outer relaxation with value \(u^*\ge v^*\). If a polynomial-time rounding method returns a feasible \(\widehat x\) satisfying \(f(\widehat x)\ge\beta u^*\) for some \(\beta\in[0,1]\), then
\[f(\widehat x)\ge\beta u^*\ge\beta v^*.\]
Thus a lower factor measured against the relaxation upper bound transfers unchanged to the original optimum. In particular, if \(f(\widehat x)\ge u^*/\delta\) for \(\delta\ge1\), then \(f(\widehat x)\ge v^*/\delta\). An additional upper bound \(u^*\le\gamma v^*\) controls the relaxation gap but is not required for this lower approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible value attaining a fraction of an outer-relaxation value attains at least the same fraction of the original maximization optimum.
assumptions_latex: The point \(\widehat x\) is feasible for the original QCQP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widehat x)\ge\beta v^*\).

notation.meaning: rounding factor relative to the relaxation value

review_flags: The implication follows directly from the order of the original and outer-relaxation optima.

children.title: Unbounded Gap Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem families lacking uniform finite gap control.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes instance families on which an additive or multiplicative relaxation discrepancy has no uniform bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of maximization QCQPs and outer relaxations has an unbounded additive gap if, for every \(M>0\), some instance satisfies \(u^*-v^*>M\). It has an unbounded multiplicative gap if, for every \(M>0\), some instance with \(0<v^*<\infty\) satisfies \(u^*/v^*>M\). In the latter regime no finite constant \(C\) can certify \(u^*\le Cv^*\) uniformly over the family, so approximation claims derived solely from such a uniform relaxation-factor bound are unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap regime is unbounded when instances make the relaxed upper bound arbitrarily farther from the finite positive QCQP optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_I(u_I^*-v_I^*)=\infty\) or \(\sup_I u_I^*/v_I^*=\infty\), according to the chosen convention.

children.title: Problem Scaling
children.top_down_role: Objective, constraint, and variable scaling choices for QCQP numerics.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses equivalent real QCQP instances obtained by invertible diagonal variable scaling and positive objective or constraint scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a real QCQP, let
\[\phi_i(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Q_i x+2a_i^{\mathsf T}x+c_i,\qquad i=0,\ldots,m,\]
where \(\phi_0\) is the objective and the constraints are \(\phi_i(x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Choose an invertible diagonal matrix \(D\), set \(x=Dy\), and choose positive scalars \(s_i\). Define
\[\widehat\phi_i(y)=s_i\phi_i(Dy)=y^{\mathsf T}(s_iD^{\mathsf T}Q_iD)y+2(s_iD^{\mathsf T}a_i)^{\mathsf T}y+s_ic_i.\]
Because \(D\) is invertible and \(s_i>0\), each constraint \(\phi_i(x)\le0\) is equivalent to \(\widehat\phi_i(y)\le0\) under \(x=Dy\). Positive scaling of the objective preserves its minimizers or maximizers and multiplies its optimal value by \(s_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible diagonal variable scaling and positive scaling of the objective and constraints give an equivalent real QCQP with corresponding solutions but different coefficient magnitudes.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is invertible and diagonal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi_i(x)\le0\iff\widehat\phi_i(D^{-1}x)\le0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and optimal solutions correspond under \(x=Dy\).

notation.meaning: original quadratic objective or constraint function

children.title: Matrix Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing of matrix magnitudes or row-column norms in quadratic data.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines positive diagonal row-column scaling that balances matrix norms before numerical QCQP solution, with compatibility and symmetry qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), matrix equilibration seeks positive diagonal matrices \(R\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) and \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) such that \(B=RAC\) has prescribed positive norms
\[\lVert B_{i:}\rVert_2=\tau_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,p),\qquad \lVert B_{:j}\rVert_2=\kappa_j\quad(j=1,\ldots,n)\]
for nonzero rows and columns. A necessary compatibility condition is
\[\sum_{i=1}^p\tau_i^2=\sum_{j=1}^n\kappa_j^2,\]
because both sides equal \(\lVert B\rVert_F^2\). Consequently, simultaneous unit row and column norms require \(p=n\), though that condition alone does not guarantee existence for every sparsity pattern. For symmetric QCQP matrices, congruence scaling \(B=C^{\mathsf T}AC\) preserves symmetry and corresponds to diagonal variable scaling. When exact targets are unattainable, approximate equilibration seeks positive diagonal scalings whose row and column norms are close to compatible targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix equilibration uses positive diagonal row and column scalings to approach compatible target norms; congruence scaling preserves symmetry for quadratic-form matrices.
assumptions_latex: The diagonal entries of \(R\) and \(C\) are strictly positive.
Zero rows and columns are excluded from positive norm targets.
Exact targets satisfy the necessary condition \(\sum_i\tau_i^2=\sum_j\kappa_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When exact equilibration exists, \(B=RAC\) satisfies \(\lVert B_{i:}\rVert_2=\tau_i\) and \(\lVert B_{:j}\rVert_2=\kappa_j\); simultaneous unit targets necessarily imply \(p=n\).

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scaling matrices
